title: [Bug]: Mattermost 10.11.17 contains 10.11.16
need_summary: Whether Mattermost 10.11.17 is actually a distinct security-fixed release or just the same as 10.11.16, based on the maintainer’s changelog link saying both are the same release and that v10.11.18 will contain the proper fix.
security_topic: release equivalence and version-specific security fix availability
question_text:
I download the version 10.11.17 after install ( upgrade) the mattermost version shows 10.11.16.
wget https://releases.mattermost.com/10.11.17/mattermost-10.11.17-linux-amd64.tar.gz
 sudo -u mattermost /opt/mattermost/bin/mattermost version
Version: 10.11.16
Build Number: 25420914588
Build Date: Wed May  6 07:19:37 UTC 2026
Build Hash: 202d125afa87fe39611686850fd82590c99ca344
Build Enterprise Ready: true


so it could be a wrong package to download , and the version have not the security fixes.
answer_text: Both v10.11.16 and v10.11.17 are the same release and safe to use: https://docs.mattermost.com/product-overview/mattermost-v10-changelog.html#release-v10-11-extended-support-release. v10.11.18 will contain a proper fix.

title: v11.3: Validate log levels in AdvancedLoggingJSON
need_summary: Whether Mattermost v11.3’s AdvancedLoggingJSON validation intentionally rejects audit log levels in standard logging and standard levels in audit logging, based on PR #34414 and the linked documentation update.
security_topic: validation rules separating standard and audit logging configuration
question_text:
@claude - Let’s update the Mattermost Product Documentation to reflect the System Admin AdvancedLoggingJSON configuration and audit logging settings product experience from Mattermost server vv11.3 onward captured via https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/34414

Scope & constraints (include non-editable docs list):
Scope: document AdvancedLoggingJSON validation rules for standard vs audit logging and the admin console label change for Audit logging; focus on config and admin UI behavior only.
Constraints: DO NOT modify changelogs, important upgrade notes, version archive, removed/deprecated features, or unsupported legacy releases.
Required doc touchpoints:
Identify likely pages for server logging configuration, AdvancedLoggingJSON examples, and audit logging settings (admin console and config.json).
Update any admin console settings labels or screenshots/text referring to “Audit logging (Beta)” where applicable.
Persona-separated tasks (System Admin only):
Explain that AdvancedLoggingJSON validation now enforces valid log level IDs and rejects audit levels in standard logging, and standard levels in audit logging; include “what changed/why/how to fix” guidance and common error symptoms (validation errors for invalid level IDs).
Clarify that audit logging uses audit-specific levels only (audit-api, audit-content, audit-permissions, audit-cli) and that standard logging rejects these levels, based on new validation behavior.
Note the admin console label change from “Audit logging (Beta)” to “Audit Logging” while beta status remains (isBeta flag), and update any UI references accordingly.
Output requirements:
Provide a list of pages/sections to update.
Provide proposed doc text snippets (before/after or insert-ready).
If PR review not possible: milestone not found in PR evidence (summary.json); a human must validate milestone/version if needed.
answer_text:
I've created **5 comprehensive documentation files** covering all aspects of the v11.3 changes:

1. **`v11.3-advancedloggingjson-changes.md`** - Technical overview of all changes
2. **`audit-logging-configuration-updates.md`** - Audit logging specific configuration  
3. **`admin-console-updates-v11.3.md`** - Admin console UI changes and screenshot updates
4. **`troubleshooting-advancedloggingjson-v11.3.md`** - Complete troubleshooting guide
5. **`documentation-update-summary.md`** - Master list of pages needing updates with insert-ready snippets

### 🔍 Key Changes Documented

**AdvancedLoggingJSON Validation Changes:**
- Standard logging (`LogSettings`) now validates against `mlog.MlvlAll` (standard levels only)  
- Audit logging (`ExperimentalAuditSettings`) now validates against `mlog.MLvlAuditAll` (audit levels only)
- Cross-contamination between logging types now triggers validation errors

**Admin Console Updates:**
- Label changed from "Audit logging (Beta)" to "Audit Logging"
- Beta status remains in backend (`isBeta` flag unchanged)

**Audit Log Levels:**
- `audit-api` (ID: 100) - REST API access
- `audit-content` (ID: 101) - Content creation  
- `audit-permissions` (ID: 102) - Permission checks
- `audit-cli` (ID: 103) - CLI operations (legacy)

Certificate is valid only for names:
- *.push.mattermost.com
- push.mattermost.com
And not valid for push-test.mattermost.com
answer_text:

DNS:*.push.mattermost.com, DNS:push-test.mattermost.com, DNS:push.mattermost.com

thread_text:
ISSUE #34589: [Bug]: "Recent mentions" button starts returning HTTP 499 error
Author: astrelczov
Date: 2025-11-25T11:06:26Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
### Before you file a bug report

- [x] I have checked the [issue tracker](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues) and have not found an issue that matches the one I'm filing.
- [x] This issue is not a troubleshooting question. Troubleshooting questions go here: https://forum.mattermost.com/c/trouble-shoot/16.
- [x] This issue is not a feature request. You can request features and make product suggestions here: https://mattermost.uservoice.com/forums/306457-general/.
- [x] This issue reproduces on one of the [currently supported server versions](https://docs.mattermost.com/about/mattermost-server-releases.html#latest-releases).
- [x] I have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Mattermost Handbook Contribution Guidelines](https://handbook.mattermost.com/contributors/contributors/guidelines/contribution-guidelines).

### Mattermost Server Version

all latest versions above 10.8

### Operating System

Web and Desktop clients and all server systems

### Steps to reproduce

After upgrading server from version 10.5.11 to latest ESR 10.11.8, the UI "Recent mentions" button starts returning HTTP 499 error (Client Closed Request) when querying `api/v4/posts/search` about 30 seconds after a user clicks it in both Web and Desktop clients. For all users, the "Recent mentions" view works normally on mobile, and the corresponding PostgreSQL queries use GIN pg_catalog.english. I’ve seen that the change to use the ‘simple’ search was introduced to address “Prevent stemming in DB search when search term is a fully quoted string” ([MM-60790](https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-60790); PR [#30214](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/30214)).

### Expected behavior

Original topic on the community forum is [here](https://forum.mattermost.com/t/clarification-on-how-the-database-search-works-in-mattermost/25492).

### Observed behavior

I’ve checked different parameters under **Keywords that trigger notifications**, and here’s what I’ve found.  

If send a POST request from a user who has selected only **Channel-wide mentions "channel", "all", "here"** in their settings to `api/v4/posts/search` and nothing else, the payload looks like:  
```
{"terms":"\"@test.user\"","is_or_search":true,"include_deleted_channels":true,"time_zone_offset":25200,"page":0,"per_page":20}
```
In this case, I get a `simple` search in the database, which doesn’t finish within the 30-second client timeout.  

However, if the same user enables any of the remaining options - for example, **Your non case-sensitive username "test.user"** - then the PostgreSQL query runs very quickly using the default `english` GIN index. The payload in this case looks like:  
```
{"terms":"\"test.user\" \"@test.user\"","is_or_search":true,"include_deleted_channels":true,"time_zone_offset":25200,"page":0,"per_page":20}
```

### Log Output

```shell
Query error searching posts. caller=“sqlstore/post_store.go:2274” error=“pq: canceling statement due to user request
```

### Additional Information

In the PostgreSQL logs, the problematic query from Web/Desktop clients looks like this:

>SELECT , (SELECT COUNT() FROM Posts WHERE Posts.RootId = (CASE WHEN q2.RootId = ‘’ THEN q2.Id ELSE q2.RootId END) AND Posts.DeleteAt = 0) as ReplyCount FROM Posts q2 WHERE q2.DeleteAt = 0 AND q2.Type NOT LIKE ‘system_%’ AND to_tsvector(‘simple’, Message) @@ **to_tsquery(‘simple’,‘“@test.user”’)** AND ChannelId IN (SELECT Id FROM Channels, ChannelMembers WHERE Id = ChannelId AND ChannelMembers.UserId = ‘{REDACTED}’) ORDER BY q2.CreateAt DESC LIMIT 100

Meanwhile, users who do not experience the issue see a different query, and their searches use a different text search configuration:

>SELECT , (SELECT COUNT() FROM Posts WHERE Posts.RootId = (CASE WHEN q2.RootId = ‘’ THEN q2.Id ELSE q2.RootId END) AND Posts.DeleteAt = 0) as ReplyCount FROM Posts q2 WHERE q2.DeleteAt = 0 AND q2.Type NOT LIKE ‘system_%’ AND to_tsvector(‘pg_catalog.english’, Message) @@ **to_tsquery(‘pg_catalog.english’,‘“@test.seconduser”’**) AND ChannelId IN (SELECT Id FROM Channels, ChannelMembers WHERE Id = ChannelId AND ChannelMembers.UserId = ‘{REDACTED}’) ORDER BY q2.CreateAt DESC LIMIT 100

### Mattermost Server Version

all latest versions above 10.8

### Operating System

Web and Desktop clients and all server systems

### Steps to reproduce

After upgrading server from version 10.5.11 to latest ESR 10.11.8, the UI "Recent mentions" button starts returning HTTP 499 error (Client Closed Request) when querying `api/v4/posts/search` about 30 seconds after a user clicks it in both Web and Desktop clients. For all users, the "Recent mentions" view works normally on mobile, and the corresponding PostgreSQL queries use GIN pg_catalog.english. I’ve seen that the change to use the ‘simple’ search was introduced to address “Prevent stemming in DB search when search term is a fully quoted string” ([MM-60790](https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-60790); PR [#30214](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/30214)).

### Expected behavior

Original topic on the community forum is [here](https://forum.mattermost.com/t/clarification-on-how-the-database-search-works-in-mattermost/25492).

### Observed behavior

I’ve checked different parameters under **Keywords that trigger notifications**, and here’s what I’ve found.  

If send a POST request from a user who has selected only **Channel-wide mentions "channel", "all", "here"** in their settings to `api/v4/posts/search` and nothing else, the payload looks like:  
```
{"terms":"\"@test.user\"","is_or_search":true,"include_deleted_channels":true,"time_zone_offset":25200,"page":0,"per_page":20}
```
In this case, I get a `simple` search in the database, which doesn’t finish within the 30-second client timeout.  

However, if the same user enables any of the remaining options - for example, **Your non case-sensitive username "test.user"** - then the PostgreSQL query runs very quickly using the default `english` GIN index. The payload in this case looks like:  
```
{"terms":"\"test.user\" \"@test.user\"","is_or_search":true,"include_deleted_channels":true,"time_zone_offset":25200,"page":0,"per_page":20}
```

### Log Output

```shell
Query error searching posts. caller=“sqlstore/post_store.go:2274” error=“pq: canceling statement due to user request
```

### Additional Information

In the PostgreSQL logs, the problematic query from Web/Desktop clients looks like this:

>SELECT , (SELECT COUNT() FROM Posts WHERE Posts.RootId = (CASE WHEN q2.RootId = ‘’ THEN q2.Id ELSE q2.RootId END) AND Posts.DeleteAt = 0) as ReplyCount FROM Posts q2 WHERE q2.DeleteAt = 0 AND q2.Type NOT LIKE ‘system_%’ AND to_tsvector(‘simple’, Message) @@ **to_tsquery(‘simple’,‘“@test.user”’)** AND ChannelId IN (SELECT Id FROM Channels, ChannelMembers WHERE Id = ChannelId AND ChannelMembers.UserId = ‘{REDACTED}’) ORDER BY q2.CreateAt DESC LIMIT 100

Meanwhile, users who do not experience the issue see a different query, and their searches use a different text search configuration:

>SELECT , (SELECT COUNT() FROM Posts WHERE Posts.RootId = (CASE WHEN q2.RootId = ‘’ THEN q2.Id ELSE q2.RootId END) AND Posts.DeleteAt = 0) as ReplyCount FROM Posts q2 WHERE q2.DeleteAt = 0 AND q2.Type NOT LIKE ‘system_%’ AND to_tsvector(‘pg_catalog.english’, Message) @@ **to_tsquery(‘pg_catalog.english’,‘“@test.seconduser”’**) AND ChannelId IN (SELECT Id FROM Channels, ChannelMembers WHERE Id = ChannelId AND ChannelMembers.UserId = ‘{REDACTED}’) ORDER BY q2.CreateAt DESC LIMIT 100

title: [Bug]: New version of docker container does not have shell
need_summary: Whether removing the shell from the Mattermost Docker image was an intentional security hardening change and the answer rests on the maintainer’s explanation that the image was moved to a distroless base to reduce attack surface.
security_topic: container hardening and health-check compatibility
question_text:
Many instance of Mattermost is running under Docker Container and possibly they use health check command to ensure the container is running and its okay.
Some tools like Coolify also use this command to wait until service become ready, then route the traffic to it.
The usual command is `curl 127.0.0.1:8065` which check for a HTTP 200 response code.
But in latest version there is no shell inside the container to run this health check command and it will be unhealthy forever.
So in tools like Coolify it wont get ready and traffic will'not route to it and it will break.

Expected behavior

Container should have shell for backward compatibility.
answer_text: Mattermost docker image no longer has shell as we moved to using a distroless image as our base build image. This significantly reduces both the attack surface and the image size. Health check is ensured by running `mmctl system status --local`

title: [Bug]: Mattermost 10.10.1 service fails to run after upgrade
need_summary: Whether Mattermost 10.10.1 should still run on older glibc systems and what version restores compatibility, anchored by the maintainer’s statement that pending v10.10.2 will restore previous GLIBC compatibility and the v10.11 extended support changelog link.
security_topic: binary compatibility with older glibc on supported Linux distributions
question_text:
### Mattermost Server Version

10.10.1

### Operating System

Rocky Linux release 8.10 (Green Obsidian)

### Steps to reproduce

- Upgrade mattermost 10.9.1 to 10.10.1 following the [Upgrade Mattermost Server](https://docs.mattermost.com/upgrade/upgrading-mattermost-server.html) documentation
- Run `systemctl start mattermost`

### Expected behavior

The mattermost service to start without any issue

### Observed behavior

Failed to start Mattermost.


### Log Output

```shell
/opt/mattermost/bin/mattermost: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.32' not found (required by /opt/mattermost/bin/mattermost)
/opt/mattermost/bin/mattermost: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found (required by /opt/mattermost/bin/mattermost)
mattermost.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
mattermost.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Failed to start Mattermost.
```
answer_text: Just a heads up, we're patching this with the pending v10.10.2 to restore our previous GLIBC compatibility. We expect this to remain supported until at least next summer, when [Debian Bullseye](https://www.debian.org/releases/bullseye/) goes out of LTS. (We may separately evaluate a strategy that supports this for longer.)

[c6] @agnivade 2025-07-22T06:42:16Z:
Thanks everyone for the report. We have looked into this. The root cause does not lie with Go version, but the builder we use to build Mattermost. 

When we build our binaries, we use a builder [Dockerfile](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/build/Dockerfile.buildenv)  to do the job. But there are multi-level vendor dependencies which complicates things, because of the need to update all parts of the toolchain.

1. When we update the Go version in that Dockerfile, we also update the OS version.
2. Now an updated OS, will have an updated toolchain version as well.
3. So when we upgraded from Go1.23-bullseye to Go1.24-bookworm, the GLIBC version got upgraded from 2.31 to 2.36. (**Note the fact that MM 10.9 still gets compiled with GLIBC 2.31 and works fine**)
4. The issue is that with GLIBC 2.34, they decided to remove libpthread, and package everything under libc: https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2021/12/17/why-glibc-234-removed-libpthread. So therefore, the default symbol versions that the linker will link against will need to change.
And that is why when you are building binaries in an environment with GLIBC >=2.34, it poses a minimum requirement when using it in other environments with older GLIBC versions.

comments.author: agnivade
comments.body:
Thanks everyone for the report. We have looked into this. The root cause does not lie with Go version, but the builder we use to build Mattermost. 

When we build our binaries, we use a builder [Dockerfile](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/build/Dockerfile.buildenv)  to do the job. But there are multi-level vendor dependencies which complicates things, because of the need to update all parts of the toolchain.

1. When we update the Go version in that Dockerfile, we also update the OS version.
2. Now an updated OS, will have an updated toolchain version as well.
3. So when we upgraded from Go1.23-bullseye to Go1.24-bookworm, the GLIBC version got upgraded from 2.31 to 2.36. (**Note the fact that MM 10.9 still gets compiled with GLIBC 2.31 and works fine**)
4. The issue is that with GLIBC 2.34, they decided to remove libpthread, and package everything under libc: https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2021/12/17/why-glibc-234-removed-libpthread. So therefore, the default symbol versions that the linker will link against will need to change.
And that is why when you are building binaries in an environment with GLIBC >=2.34, it poses a minimum requirement when using it in other environments with older GLIBC versions.

Start container docker-compose up -d 4. Observe docker logs screen is attached for logs 5. Error appears in logs repeatedly: Failed to ping DB error setting up connections: stat /home/nonroot/.postgresql/postgresql.crt: permission denied 6. answer_text: Hi all, a note from our team: Looks like the Postgres inside the container can’t access the cert file - Postgres runs with UID ``70`` inside the container, so a ``chown -R 70:70 /home/nonroot/.postgresql/`` might fix the issue.

title: [Bug]: mmctl export create fails with 'Limit exceeded for paging'
need_summary: Whether mmctl export create requires MariaDB 10.5+ because JSON_ARRAYAGG is missing on older versions, as shown by the linked MariaDB JSON_ARRAYAGG documentation.
security_topic: database-version compatibility causing export failure
answer_text:
### The problem

MariaDB versions before 10.5.0 do no support JSON_ARRAYAGG [[source](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-functions/special-functions/json-functions/json_arrayagg)]. This is required for `mmctl export` to work.

### The solution

Temporarily switch Mattermost to a newer MariaDB. You could upgrade in-place, but that seemed dangerous to me.

@archiekennedy 2025-07-28T12:36:47Z: Problem solved in this thread https://forum.mattermost.com/t/mmctl-export-create-fails-with-limit-exceeded-for-paging/23485 ✔️ Reposting here for posterity: ### The problem MariaDB versions before 10.5.0 do no support JSON_ARRAYAGG [[source](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-functions/special-functions/json-functions/json_arrayagg)]. This is required for `mmctl export` to work. ### The solution Temporarily switch Mattermost to a newer MariaDB. You could upgrade in-place, but that seemed dangerous to me. #### Set up a new MariaDB server I created a Debian 12 server, which is new enough to install MariaDB 10.11.11. 1. Install MariaDB on a new server: ``` # root@new-server apt update apt install mariadb-server ``` 2. Configure it to listen to remote connections: Edit `/etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf` ```diff # Instead of skip-networking the default is now to listen only on # localhost which is more compatible and is not less secure. - bind-address = 127.0.0.1 + bind-address = 0.0.0.0 ``` 3. Restart MariaDB: ``` service mariadb restart ``` 4. If using a firewall you might need to open the MariaDB port, for example: ``` ufw allow 3306/tcp ufw reload ``` 6. Prepare the Mattermost database (you need to use the **same** DB user password as your original instance, replace 'db_user_password') ``` # root@new-server mysql ``` ```sql CREATE DATABASE mattermost; CREATE USER 'mattermost'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'db_user_password'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON mattermost.* TO 'mattermost'@'%'; ``` #### Copy the data across 1. On the old server, perform a database dump: ``` # root@old-server mysqldump mattermost > mattermost_dump.sql ``` 2. Copy the `mattermost_dump.sql` file to the new server. 3. On the new server, restore the data: ``` # Note: I'm logging in with the 'mattermost' database user and requesting a password # prompt with '-p'. This isn't strictly necessary ('mysql mattermost' would work) but # it's a nice test that the user has the right permissions. cat mattermost_dump.sql | mysql -u mattermost -p mattermost ``` #### Switch Mattermost to the new MariaDB server 1. On the old server, edit the Mattermost config `/opt/mattermost/config/config.json` – replacing 'db_user_password' and 'my_db_ip_address'. ```diff "SqlSettings": { "DriverName": "mysql", - "DataSource": "mattermost:db_user_password@tcp(localhost:58103)/mattermost?charset=utf8mb4,utf8\u0026readTimeout=30s\u0026writeTimeout=30s", + "DataSource": "mattermost:db_user_password@tcp(my_db_ip_address:58103)/mattermost?charset=utf8mb4,utf8\u0026readTimeout=30s\u0026writeTimeout=30s", "DataSourceReplicas": [], ``` 2. Restart Mattermost: ``` service mattermost restart ``` #### Final result At this point your set up looks like this: And you are free to run `mmctl export create` 🙂 ---

need_summary: Whether the Playbooks v1 plugin’s enterprise-license requirement in Mattermost 10.5.6 was a known issue fixed in Playbooks v1.41.1, as referenced by the linked release tag.
security_topic: plugin license-gating causing unexpected activation failure after upgrade

thread_text:
ISSUE #31167: [Bug]: Without Enterprise license MM 10.5.6 refuses to activate Playbooks v1 plugin
Author: clpab
Date: 2025-05-23T11:07:19Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
### Before you file a bug report

- [x] I have checked the [issue tracker](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues) and have not found an issue that matches the one I'm filing.
- [x] This issue is not a troubleshooting question. Troubleshooting questions go here: https://forum.mattermost.com/c/trouble-shoot/16.
- [x] This issue is not a feature request. You can request features and make product suggestions here: https://mattermost.uservoice.com/forums/306457-general/.
- [x] This issue reproduces on one of the [currently supported server versions](https://docs.mattermost.com/about/mattermost-server-releases.html#latest-releases).
- [x] I have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Mattermost Handbook Contribution Guidelines](https://handbook.mattermost.com/contributors/contributors/guidelines/contribution-guidelines).

### Mattermost Server Version

10.5.6 ESR

### Operating System

RHEL 8

### Steps to reproduce

Upgrade Mattermost Free edition from 9.11.* to 10.5.6 according to the documentation.

Additional notes:
- Back in March I tested the upgrade from 9.11.* to 10.5.2. With this version, Playbooks v1 plugin was still working fine.
- There is nothing mentioned in V10.5.3 - 6 release notes, that v1 Playbooks will no longer work.
- I have not tested Upgrading from 10.5.* to 10.5.6.

### Expected behavior

For non-customers using the free version of Mattermost, Playbooks v1 can be used uninterrupted through Mattermost v10 until Mattermost v11 is released (estimated around September 2025).

This was confirmed by Mattermost staff back in October 2024:
https://forum.mattermost.com/t/clarification-on-playbooks-in-mattermost-v10/20563

### Observed behavior

Playbooks v1 Plugin is no longer working.
Errors are written to "mattermost.log", stating the plugin is unable to activate due to missing Enterprise license.

### Log Output

```shell
{"timestamp":"2025-05-22 20:25:14.562 +02:00","level":"error","msg":"Failed to install prepackaged plugin","caller":"app/plugin.go:975","bundle_path":"/opt/mattermost/prepackaged_plugins/mattermost-plugin-playbooks-v1.41.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz","error":"Failed to install extracted prepackaged plugin /opt/mattermost/prepackaged_plugins/mattermost-plugin-playbooks-v1.41.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz: installExtractedPlugin: Unable to restart plugin on upgrade., this plugin requires an enterprise license"}
{"timestamp":"2025-05-22 20:25:15.385 +02:00","level":"error","msg":"Unable to activate plugin","caller":"app/plugin.go:144","plugin_id":"playbooks","bundle_path":"plugins/playbooks","error":"this plugin requires an enterprise license"}
```

### Additional Information

None.

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @VincentSC 2025-05-23T13:58:50Z:
Got the same. The Playbooks plugin 1.41.0 requires a license, while 1.40.0 does not. Besides the log, it can also be seen at `Plugin Management` of the System Console.

For me that was the upgrade from MM 10.8.0 to 10.8.1. I assume that 10.5.6 includes plugin version 1.41.0 and 10.5.5 has 1.40.0.

I fixed it, by downgrading to 10.8.0
---
[c2] @cloudgitaware 2025-05-26T12:33:06Z:
I have this issue after upgrading to version 10.8.1 free edition. I can see the playbook data still in the database but i have the "this plugin requires an enterprise license" for "mattermost-plugin-playbooks-v1.41.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
When reading https://forum.mattermost.com/t/clarification-on-playbooks-in-mattermost-v10/20563 i see that "For Non-Customers: For non-customers using the free version of Mattermost, Playbooks v1 can be used uninterrupted through Mattermost v10"

Can we please clarify whether this is no longer the case or whether we need to wait for a fix?
---
[c3] @clpab 2025-05-26T14:56:56Z:
I got it back working as follows (try at your own risk after doing a backup):
1) Disabled "Playbooks" plugin in Mattermost
2) Stopped Mattermost service
3) Removed prepackaged plugin files (e.g. "rm /opt/mattermost/prepackaged_plugins/mattermost-plugin-playbooks*")
4) Overwrote current Playbooks plugin directory (e.g. /opt/mattermost/plugins/playbooks) with freshly downloaded plugin package (e.g. "tar -zxvf mattermost-plugin-playbooks-v1.41.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz")
5) Started Mattermost service
6) Activated "Playbooks" plugin in Mattermost

I hope this will be fixed for upcoming V10 updates.
---
[c4] @amyblais 2025-06-17T12:21:56Z:
This was fixed earlier in Playbooks v1.41.1 https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-plugin-playbooks/releases/tag/v1.41.1. The version will also be pre-packaged to upcoming server dot releases.
---

When you hover over a URL within a channel on desktop, browser and client, it will remove your user input cursor from the focus, meaning you cannot type or paste into the channel without manually clicking the box again

title: Messages not showing until quit+reopen app
need_summary: Whether the missed-message behavior is caused by a server websocket timeout that eventually reconnects after about 15 minutes, anchored on the maintainer’s explanation and linked PR https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/27846 plus the server ticket MM-60225.
security_topic: missed messages due to websocket or cluster delivery issue
question_text: Almost every 1-2 days, I and other users in my organisation do not receive sent direct messages (maybe tags in channels too). Quitting the desktop application and re-opening it will then show unread messages that were previously not visible.
answer_text: The good news is that it might already be fixed, IF you're in a clustered environment: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/27846. Recently we discovered that due to some caching issues on the server users were not sent the message to be added to the channel, due to a miss in the cluster sending code where the cache was invalidated AFTER the message was supposed to be sent.

I have managed to find a way to reproduce this systematically. It is caused by a network change between client and server. It applies to both desktop and web version.

1. Open two mattermost clients (e.g. desktop and web) that are connected to the same server.
2. Change your network connection. NB: not all network changes trigger this. For example, simply reconnecting did not trigger it for me, nor did switching from a wired connection to a connection tethered from my phone. What did trigger it was a change in my vpn connection (switching back to a legacy config or from there to the newer one). I suspect it's due to this changing my IP from the perspective of the server.
3. Refresh one of your clients (ctrl-r works on desktop)
4. See new messages and notifications come in on the refreshed client, but not on the non-refreshed client.

comments.author: setpill
comments.body:
I have managed to find a way to reproduce this systematically. It is caused by a network change between client and server. It applies to both desktop and web version.

1. Open two mattermost clients (e.g. desktop and web) that are connected to the same server.
2. Change your network connection. NB: not all network changes trigger this. For example, simply reconnecting did not trigger it for me, nor did switching from a wired connection to a connection tethered from my phone. What did trigger it was a change in my vpn connection (switching back to a legacy config or from there to the newer one). I suspect it's due to this changing my IP from the perspective of the server.
3. Refresh one of your clients (ctrl-r works on desktop)
4. See new messages and notifications come in on the refreshed client, but not on the non-refreshed client.

title: Gitlab SSO requires full api scope
need_summary: Whether Mattermost’s GitLab SSO scope should be configured to read_user instead of full api, based on the documented GitLabSettings.Scope setting in the Mattermost GitLab SSO docs.
security_topic: GitLab SSO OAuth scope configuration
question_text: GitLab SSO requires full api scope instead of only read_user as the docs state.
answer_text:
Setting this to `read_user` was enough to get it working in team edition.

It doesn't look like there's any way to set this parameter from within the Mattermost web UI, or with environment variables (at least [not documented here](https://docs.mattermost.com/configure/authentication-configuration-settings.html#gitlab-oauth-2-0-settings)).

The only way to set it is by editing `config.json` manually, and restarting the server.
thread_text:
ISSUE #28047: Gitlab SSO requires full api scope
Author: maritz
Date: 2024-08-25T12:37:53Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
GitLab SSO requires full api scope instead of only read_user as the docs state.

#### Steps to reproduce
- Set up GitLab SSO and don't check the "api" scope when creating the application in GitLab
- Try to switch a user (or make a new one) to GitLab SSO

#### Mattermost Server Version
Mattermost Version: 9.11.0

#### Expected behavior
SSO should work (as it does when selecting the api scope)

#### Observed behavior
GitLab page with error message: "The requested scope is invalid, unknown, or malformed."

#### Log Output
Can provide some later, if needed.

#### Possible fixes
Reduce the requested scope to read_user as suggested here: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/287946#note_453774032
(also in that issue thread is another mattermost user experiencing the same issue)


The full api scope provides too much access and thus poses a security problem.


--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @micolous 2024-10-02T04:54:01Z:
I saw the same issue trying to set up GitLab auth on a fresh team edition install.

I was missing a `GitLabSettings.Scope` configuration (noted in ["Step 2: Configure Mattermost for GitLab SSO"](https://docs.mattermost.com/onboard/sso-gitlab.html#step-2-configure-mattermost-for-gitlab-sso), 7th item) – and the default is to set this to `""` (empty string).

Setting this to `read_user` was enough to get it working in team edition.

It doesn't look like there's any way to set this parameter from within the Mattermost web UI, or with environment variables (at least [not documented here](https://docs.mattermost.com/configure/authentication-configuration-settings.html#gitlab-oauth-2-0-settings)).

The only way to set it is by editing `config.json` manually, and restarting the server.

Exposing this parameter to the web UI ([suggested in another report for this issue](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues/17499#issuecomment-978814072)) seems like an easy way to address this class of issue 😉 

---
[c2] @maritz 2024-10-02T21:40:57Z:
Alright, consider me blind. I missed that part of the documentation. Works with the change @micolous suggested.

Don't know if you want to keep this open for the suggestion of micolous about making that value a UI changeable value. Otherwise this can be closed.
---

title: Prevent HEAD requests to a sub-path from returning a 302
need_summary: Whether the infinite redirect on HEAD requests to a Mattermost sub-path is fixed by adding HEAD handling to `w.MainRouter.Handle("/{anything:.*}", w.NewStaticHandler(root)).Methods(http.MethodGet, http.MethodHead)` in `server/channels/web/static.go`.
security_topic: HEAD request redirect loop on subpath handling
question_text:
If we return a 302 for a HEAD request, then it goes into an infinite redirect. The fix should be to simply return a 200 like we do for GET requests.

You can use the utils.GetSubpathFromConfig to check if there's a subpath or not, and then simply return a 200 instead of 302.
answer_text:
Great investigation @Aryakoste! I think we just forgot to add the `HEAD` handling for the route above. The following fixes the problem.

```diff
diff --git a/server/channels/web/static.go b/server/channels/web/static.go
index 04e9857142..91cbae42af 100644
--- a/server/channels/web/static.go
+++ b/server/channels/web/static.go
@@ -47,7 +47,7 @@ func (w *Web) InitStatic() {
                w.MainRouter.PathPrefix("/static/").Handler(staticHandler)
                w.MainRouter.Handle("/robots.txt", http.HandlerFunc(robotsHandler))
                w.MainRouter.Handle("/unsupported_browser.js", http.HandlerFunc(unsupportedBrowserScriptHandler))
-               w.MainRouter.Handle("/{anything:.*}", w.NewStaticHandler(root)).Methods(http.MethodGet)
+               w.MainRouter.Handle("/{anything:.*}", w.NewStaticHandler(root)).Methods(http.MethodGet, http.MethodHead)

                // When a subpath is defined, it's necessary to handle redirects without a
                // trailing slash. We don't want to use StrictSlash on the w.MainRouter and affect
```

title: Enabling Automatic replies does not immediately change status to 'Out of Office' anymore
need_summary: Whether the initial Out of Office status bug was fixed by PR #29371, and the maintainer also points to separate issue MM-61438 plus the `/api/v4/users/statuses/ids` behavior as the source for the remaining multi-server inconsistency.
security_topic: status update delay after enabling automatic replies
question_text:
Steps to reproduce:

1. Go to Settings > Notifications > Automatic direct message replies
1. Enable this setting

Expected

- As the help text suggests “Enabling Automatic Replies sets your status to Out of Office and disables email and push notifications.” I expect this to happen immediately.

Observed

- My status did not immediately get changed to `Out of Office` and I stayed `Online`. After waiting roughly 30 seconds, it did then change my status for me.
- If I refresh, my status is set to `Out of Office` immediately.



Tested on Community (9.11.0) and Hub (9.10.1)
answer_text:
Looking at it, the bug in the initial report likely got fixed by https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/29371.

What you're seeing with the user coming back online on Community is a separate issue (https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-61438) which I was just able to confirm still reproduces, so thanks for mentioning you saw that on Community. On Community, I set my alt account to out of office, and if I repeatedly request my status from `/api/v4/users/statuses/ids`, I get responses alternating between online and OOO, so there's clearly an issue there.

Thanks for looking into this since it helped me realize where the other issue is happening. I'm going to close this issue as the main bug in this ticket is fixed, and we have a separate ticket to address the multi-server case. We'll have to fix that one ourselves since multi-server requires EE to use.

security_topic: web client notification delivery failure on Safari
question_text: Notifications not working or not working properly depending on the browser in web client on Mac
answer_text: 3. Notifications not working in Safari (MM-59416) - This is fixed in v9.10.1 coming soon and v9.11 coming in August. This fix has also been deployed to our community server.
thread_text:
ISSUE #27534: Notifications not working in web client on Mac
Author: MJegorovas
Date: 2024-07-03T15:14:42Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
Notifications not working or not working properly depending on the browser in web client on Mac
macOS: 14.4 (23E214)
Safari: Version 17.4 (19618.1.15.11.12)
Firefox: 127.0.2 (64-bit)
Mattermost:
Mattermost Version: 9.10.0
Database Schema Version: 121
Build Number: 9664905391
Database: postgres

#### Steps to reproduce
Enable notification permission in any browser on Mac and try to get notification to show

#### Expected behavior
Notifications show up in notification centre and play a sound

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 
Safari:
No notification in centre or sound.
Well, actually there are very rare occurrences that either notification played a sound or I even got a notification in notification centre, but it is extremely rare.
Firefox:
No notification in centre, but it does play sound every time.
Found out this is because notification settings were turned off for Firefox in system settings and after enabling them I got a bit different behaviour - now every time I got notification I would get 2 sounds: 1 by mattermost and 1 by default system but again, no notification in the centre.

#### Possible fixes
For Safari, my basic debugging showed that even after granting notification permission, the moment mattermost tries to send a notification and executes this [line](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/90534b13cfd394936d14e659a390c971fd739164/webapp/channels/src/utils/notifications.ts#L70), it returns error `Notification prompting can only be done from a user gesture` so notification does not get sent. `Notification.permission` that is checked before returns granted, so I don't know why ask for permission again.

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @hmhealey 2024-07-10T16:18:44Z:
Thanks for the feedback, @MJegorovas! There's definitely a bunch of stuff we should look at here.

It sounds like there's a few different things going on here:

1. On Safari, we're failing to request the user's permission correctly. That should've been fixed in 9.10.0 by https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/26849 which would make it so that the user is prompted for permission before receiving a new message. Do you see the bar asking for that permission?

    If not, could you open a new tab, open the JS console, and check what the value of `Notification.permission` is?
    
2. On Firefox, the notification not appearing in the Notification Centre is an odd one. Looking at the code, I think the issue is actually because of some very old logic for automatically closing notifications back before that was controlled by the OS. We should be good to just remove that logic now.

3. On Firefox, I think the doubled up notification sound is a long-running UX issue. Firefox doesn't let us disable the system sound, so we'd have either have to have the user disable their OS notification sound manually or disable the MM notification sound.

---

@abhijit-singh Any suggestion on how we might fix the third one? To summarize the above, if you have desktop notification sounds enabled on Firefox on Mac, you head both the MM notification sound as well as one from MacOS
---
[c2] @hmhealey 2024-07-10T18:29:27Z:
Because I like linking things, here's a ticket for the second issue I listed above (https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-59404) and for the third one (https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-59403).

I need some more details on the first one before I can look at fixing it
---
[c3] @MJegorovas 2024-07-11T06:48:01Z:
> On Safari, we're failing to request the user's permission correctly. That should've been fixed in 9.10.0 by https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/26849 which would make it so that the user is prompted for permission before receiving a new message. Do you see the bar asking for that permission?

Yes I do, this is the behaviour after granting it. Had more comments, but I see that in the issue you've got everything figured out.
---
[c4] @hmhealey 2024-07-11T19:04:55Z:
Thanks for confirming. Given we're finding that there's more issues here than we'd expected, I'm glad that that seems to cover everything you saw on Safari 😅
---
[c5] @hmhealey 2024-07-16T15:56:10Z:
Okay, to summarize the issues reported here:
1. MM notification sounds overlapping OS ones (MM-59315) - This is not fixed yet, but we're talking to the UX team about how that should be handled in cases where we can't prevent the OS notification sound from playing.
2. Notifications not appearing in notification center (MM-59404) - This is fixed in v10.0 coming in September. The fix has already been deployed to https://community.mattermost.com.
3. Notifications not working in Safari (MM-59416) - This is fixed in v9.10.1 coming soon and v9.11 coming in August. This fix has also been deployed to our community server.

Because the more critical issues with notifications just not working have been fixed, I'm going to close this issue, but feel free to reopen this if those issues reoccur.

Thanks again for reporting this! We need to get someone on the team to use Safari as their regular browser so we can catch this sort of issue sooner
---

title: Bot mentions do not work
need_summary: Whether mentions inside webhook attachment fields trigger notifications in Mattermost, with the answer anchored on MM-59854 and the explanation that only `text` fields trigger mentions while `fields.value` does not.
security_topic: mention notification behavior in webhook attachments
question_text: When a bot user mentions another user via `@NAME`, `@here` or `@channel` they do not receive a notification.
answer_text:
IIRC, mentions in the `text` field should trigger a notification. Mentions in the `fields.value` fields do not.

I'm open to debating whether or not they should. Please note that, AFAIK, it has been this way forever :tm:.

title: Wasabi S3 Backend File Upload Problem
need_summary: Whether the Wasabi S3 upload failure is fixed by enabling `options.SendContentMd5 = true` in `s3PutOptions()`, as referenced in issue #22221 and the linked Mattermost source line.
security_topic: S3 upload compatibility with Wasabi checksum validation
question_text:
Recently some regions on Wasabi started to give an error when uploading files on Mattermost. The error is this:

Value for x-amz-checksum-crc32c header is invalid.
answer_text:
After add an option `options.SendContentMd5 = true` in [s3PutOptions()](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/a316dfb80be425aa8e6e0a965c720671a15b1e6a/server/platform/shared/filestore/s3store.go#L758-L767), it works now. Tested with v7.0.59 and v7.0.67, both works on well.
reference: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues/22221
thread_text:

You can verify this issue by simply connection any Wasabi bucket as S3 backend storage to a Mattermost installation and trying to upload a file.

title: Expired APT repository key
need_summary: Whether the Mattermost APT repository signing key expiration is a security-relevant package verification issue, with the answer anchored by the EXPKEYSIG F8F2C31744774B28 error and the linked duplicate comment.
security_topic: expired APT repository signing key
question_text:
#### Summary
The APT repository for Mattermost is currently broken (expired APT repository key)

#### Steps to reproduce
Install the APT repository using this command:
`curl -o- https://deb.packages.mattermost.com/setup-repo.sh | sudo bash`
Try to install mattermost or mattermost-desktop:
`sudo apt install mattermost`

#### Expected behavior
Mattermost should be installed as a Debian/Ubuntu package.

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 
I get this error message:
`W: An error occurred during the signature verification. The repository is not updated and the previous index files will be used. GPG error: https://deb.packages.mattermost.com focal InRelease: The following signatures were invalid: EXPKEYSIG F8F2C31744774B28 Mattermost Build <dev-ops@mattermost.com>
W: Failed to fetch https://deb.packages.mattermost.com/dists/focal/InRelease  The following signatures were invalid: EXPKEYSIG F8F2C31744774B28 Mattermost Build <dev-ops@mattermost.com>
W: Some index files failed to download. They have been ignored, or old ones used instead.`


#### Possible fixes
The signing key for the APT repository is expired and should be renewed.
answer_text: Closing as a duplicate of https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues/26707#issuecomment-2042582796.

title: Attempting to create a team with the URL of an existing team shows the wrong error message
need_summary: Whether the team URL existence check should still reveal that a URL is taken for non-admin users, with the answer resting on PR 12130 and the linked permission-based security fix for guest users.
security_topic: error-message leakage from team URL existence check
question_text:
Observed: The error message reads “Must call update for existing team.”
Expected: The error message reads “A team with that URL already exists.”
answer_text: Because of that, I think it's fine to still use "A team with this URL already exists" in this case
thread_text:
ISSUE #26841: Attempting to create a team with the URL of an existing team shows the wrong error message
Author: hmhealey
Date: 2024-04-22T14:38:08Z
Labels: Difficulty/1:Easy, Tech/ReactJS, PR Exists
State: closed

[c0]
Repro steps:

1. Click on the header of the channel list in the sidebar of the web app
2. Click on Create Team
3. On the Team Name scree, enter anything and click Next
4. On the Team URL screen, change the URL to be the URL of an existing team
5. Click Finish

Observed: The error message reads “Must call update for existing team.”
![image-20240416-175228](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/assets/3277310/f395c0bb-57c6-4be8-a899-4f20a7759e7f)
Expected: The error message reads “A team with that URL already exists.”

---

To do this, we should have the web app intercept the existing error message by its ID and show the more friendly error message instead.

----
If you're interested please comment here and come [join our "Contributors" community channel](https://community.mattermost.com/core/channels/tickets) on our daily build server, where you can discuss questions with community members and the Mattermost core team. For technical advice or questions, please  [join our "Developers" community channel](https://community.mattermost.com/core/channels/developers).

New contributors please see our [Developer's Guide](https://developers.mattermost.com/contribute/getting-started/).

JIRA: https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-57877

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @MeHow25 2024-04-23T18:02:28Z:
@hmhealey I was trying to reproduce this bug accordingly to your description and for me it shows a different error message. I added a screenshot of the message at the bottom. Honestly, for me it looks quite friendly. What do you think?

Can you also tell me what version of Mattermost are you using here? I'm using Mattermost Team Edition with the latest master branch.

![image](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/assets/61119231/83305130-9f51-4830-8405-f24ae218917c)

---
[c2] @hmhealey 2024-04-24T17:14:57Z:
I also saw the "This URL is taken" error message when I just tested on my admin account, but I see the incorrect error message on my other account, so there's something else going on here. It seems like either there's something here caused by incorrect permissions or perhaps it has to do with being on that other team.

Hopefully that gives you something to work off of, but let me know if neither of those end up being the issue, and I can take another look.

Also, if it still matters, I'm on the latest master branch as well
---
[c3] @MeHow25 2024-04-25T17:53:46Z:
@hmhealey thanks for a hint about permissions. I found a way to recreate this behavior.

Here are the steps to reproduce the bug:
1. Create User No. 1.
2. Create a team with the URL “/lorem” using that user, but do not invite anyone.
3. Create User No. 2.
4. As User No. 2, attempt to create a new team with the same URL “/lorem.”
5. An error message stating “Must call update for existing team” will be displayed.

Now I'm trying to fix the issue.
---
[c4] @MeHow25 2024-04-27T17:14:38Z:
@hmhealey I believe I've identified the code responsible for this issue. The `team.go` file contains a `teamExists` function that checks if the name of a new team is available or already taken, but I'm puzzled by its logic. Not only does it verify the team name, but it also checks if the current user has access to that team if it exists. If the user lacks access, the function returns false, implying the team doesn't exist. Shouldn't it return true instead?

I'm curious about this because the `teamExists` function is invoked during team creation and it's causing this issue.

Here is the link to this function:
https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/8348acac49198422d4762abf6d8dab29ffa21a4a/server/channels/api4/team.go#L1237
---
[c5] @hmhealey 2024-04-30T22:23:24Z:
Looking back further, that permission check goes back to https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/12130 which is to fix a minor security issue where guest users could figure out if a team exists using that endpoint when they shouldn't have been able to. Unfortunately, that makes it so that the `teamExists` API is kind of useless for what it's supposed to do.

Since I don't think we can change the API to make that more helpful, I guess the next best thing would be to detect the "must call update" error in the frontend and show a nicer error message to the end user. There's an error ID that you could use for that.

How does that sound?

---

Also, CC @jespino in case he has any ideas for how to make that API more useful again for non-admin, non-guest users
---
[c6] @MeHow25 2024-05-01T18:29:09Z:
@hmhealey Sure. The error on the frontend side comes from this line of code where we are calling the endpoint to create a team: 
https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/978f335925b91a3e92c87766caf4f4a638d0760b/webapp/channels/src/components/create_team/components/team_url/team_url.tsx#L169

I'm just not sure what should be the error message here. Wouldn't `A team with that URL already exists` also cause the same security issue? Maybe it should be something more general like `You cannot use this URL`? 
---
[c7] @hmhealey 2024-05-03T16:37:40Z:
That's a good point. I guess the difference here is that the `createTeam` endpoint requires stricter permissions than `teamExists`, and guests shouldn't have that permission so they'd get a "permission denied" before they could find if a team with that URL exists.

Because of that, I think it's fine to still use "A team with this URL already exists" in this case
---

comments.author: MeHow25
comments.body:
@hmhealey thanks for a hint about permissions. I found a way to recreate this behavior.

Here are the steps to reproduce the bug:
1. Create User No. 1.
2. Create a team with the URL “/lorem” using that user, but do not invite anyone.
3. Create User No. 2.
4. As User No. 2, attempt to create a new team with the same URL “/lorem.”
5. An error message stating “Must call update for existing team” will be displayed.

Now I'm trying to fix the issue.

comments.author: MeHow25
comments.body:
@hmhealey I believe I've identified the code responsible for this issue. The `team.go` file contains a `teamExists` function that checks if the name of a new team is available or already taken, but I'm puzzled by its logic. Not only does it verify the team name, but it also checks if the current user has access to that team if it exists. If the user lacks access, the function returns false, implying the team doesn't exist. Shouldn't it return true instead?

I'm curious about this because the `teamExists` function is invoked during team creation and it's causing this issue.

Here is the link to this function:
https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/8348acac49198422d4762abf6d8dab29ffa21a4a/server/channels/api4/team.go#L1237

comments.author: hmhealey
comments.body:
Looking back further, that permission check goes back to https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/12130 which is to fix a minor security issue where guest users could figure out if a team exists using that endpoint when they shouldn't have been able to. Unfortunately, that makes it so that the `teamExists` API is kind of useless for what it's supposed to do.

Since I don't think we can change the API to make that more helpful, I guess the next best thing would be to detect the "must call update" error in the frontend and show a nicer error message to the end user. There's an error ID that you could use for that.

How does that sound?

---

Also, CC @jespino in case he has any ideas for how to make that API more useful again for non-admin, non-guest users

comments.author: MeHow25
hmhealey
comments.body:
That's a good point. I guess the difference here is that the `createTeam` endpoint requires stricter permissions than `teamExists`, and guests shouldn't have that permission so they'd get a "permission denied" before they could find if a team with that URL exists.

Because of that, I think it's fine to still use "A team with this URL already exists" in this case

title: Plugin Token Auth Failing
need_summary: Whether the plugin HTTP request authentication bug is caused by comparing the wrong CSRF token source, with the proposed fix anchored by commit 9957c6dbd34c10573a0de4311f265928550638d9 and the referenced plugin_requests.go code path.
security_topic: plugin request authentication via CSRF token handling
question_text:
#### Summary
Token authorization is not working correctly when making plugin HTTP requests.

#### Steps to reproduce
Create a plugin that uses ServeHTTP and then make a request to that endpoint from the plugin's webapp.

#### Expected behavior
I expect the request to authenticate correctly and provide a `Mattermost-User-Id` header that I can then use to figure out who the current user is. (see discussion here: https://community.mattermost.com/core/pl/x95rjkxmobfitkbtzzox7rdxjc)

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 
The user fails to authorize because the CSRF token doesn't appear to be compared correctly.

-----------------------------

I've created a plugin that uses ServeHTTP on the server side to accept incoming API requests. Then on the webapp side I've created a button to send requests to the API endpoint I've set up. Per discussion [here](https://community.mattermost.com/core/pl/x95rjkxmobfitkbtzzox7rdxjc) it looks like my outgoing API request from the webapp should attach some kind of authentication. The server should then validate the authentication and provide a `Mattermost-User-Id` header that I can use to figure out who the user is who is making the request.

This all seems to work up to a point.

From what I can tell this comparison https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/0a496107d5ddd05fb658767fe268e2862925f7e4/server/channels/app/plugin_requests.go#L170 fails because the `sentToken` variable resolves to an empty string. However I can see in the request headers when I make the request from the webapp to the server that the request is including the correct CSRF token in the cookie (key is `MMCSRF`), the token just isn't being used in the code.

From what I can tell, the CSRF token being passed in the cookies should be accessible by calling `r.Cookie(model.SessionCookieCsrf)`. If that is compared to the `session.GetCSRF()` token then I believe the auth should succeed.

I'm happy to test this out and make a PR but I don't really know anything about the auth schema beyond 10 minutes troubleshooting this file, so I don't want to break anything.
answer_text:
@amyblais I've fixed this locally to be able to continue with my plugin development. Would I be able to submit a PR for this? It's a pretty minimal change -- https://github.com/TheStu/mattermost/commit/9957c6dbd34c10573a0de4311f265928550638d9

I see that no one has been assigned the issue in Atlassian and it would be great to get this fixed so that I can get my plugin working on a production server :)

title: 9.6.0 - Console Users display: There was an error loading the data, please try again
need_summary: Whether Mattermost’s user report failure is caused by unsupported MariaDB 10.6.16, relying on the documented database requirements page and the maintainer’s confirmation that MariaDB is not supported.
security_topic: database compatibility causing admin console failure
question_text: Since upgrade to 9.6.0 (from 9.5.2), System Console -> Users now shows "There was an error loading the data, please try again" instead of the user's list.
answer_text:
@amyblais As the community member states above we don't support MariaDB anymore, and this feature doesn't really support MySQL either, to which MariaDB is a fork of.

I think we can close this as per their comment.

title: Update 9.4 and after are breaking focalboard

title: SQL errors after upgrade from 9.3.0 to 9.4.0
need_summary: Whether the SQL scan error caused by NULL `schemeguest` values in `ChannelMembers` is safe to remediate by setting them to false, based on the maintainer’s concrete fix `UPDATE ChannelMembers SET SchemeGuest = false WHERE SchemeGuest IS NULL;` and the confirmed table/schema output.
security_topic: database repair for NULL boolean values causing channel access failures
question_text: Is it safe to run that `UPDATE ChannelMembers SET SchemeGuest = false WHERE SchemeGuest IS NULL;` and it will not break anything in the future?
answer_text: If anything it's half broken now. Yes it should be safe, but as usual with any DB operation, a backup is always recommended.
thread_text:
ISSUE #25849: SQL errors after upgrade from 9.3.0 to 9.4.0
Author: TwizzyDizzy
Date: 2024-01-04T22:27:25Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
After an upgrade from 9.3.0 to 9.4.0, some channels do not load in the UI, showing only "Loading..." but not showing any channel content.

This affects SOME channels, BUT NOT ALL channels. It does not SEEM (I cannot say for sure, as I didn't clean the app's caches / storage to verify) to affect loading the same channel on the Android app.

#### Steps to reproduce
I am currently not certain, whether this is reproducable by an upgrade from `9.3.0` to `9.4.0` or whether this is due to my database structure or content.

#### Expected behavior
Channel should be loading and showing content

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 
Spinning circle with the text "Loading..." animation

#### Possible fixes
I currently have no idea yet. But here are the logs from the Mattermost process that show up, when opening such a channel in the UI..

Also, feel free to direct me to dump my database content, so you can maybe see whether my database is corrupted, possibly (but not necessarily) by historic database migrations.

```
error [2024-01-04 23:26:42.937 +01:00] Unable to get the channel member.             caller="web/context.go:115" path=/api/v4/users/14ocq7hp3by9ic95f7zqr1mjcw/channels/girsg48543bqteppqphy97xhuw/posts/unread request_id=u1g9cyuub7n9zqt1m47m8gs5ky ip_addr=127.0.0.1 user_id=14ocq7hp3by9ic95f7zqr1mjcw method=GET err_where=getChannelMemberOnly http_code=500 error="getChannelMemberOnly: Unable to get the channel member., failed to get ChannelMember with channelId=girsg48543bqteppqphy97xhuw and userId=14ocq7hp3by9ic95f7zqr1mjcw: sql: Scan error on column index 13, name "schemeguest": sql/driver: couldn't convert <nil> (<nil>) into type bool"
```

#### Additional information
OS: Debian 12
Database: PostgreSQL 15
Architecture: x86_64


--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @streamer45 2024-01-05T14:27:46Z:
@TwizzyDizzy Would you be able to confirm your current schema and the data for the specific entry failing?

Using `psql` client you can run:

```
\d+ channelmembers;
```

And

```sql
SELECT * FROM ChannelMembers WHERE ChannelId = 'girsg48543bqteppqphy97xhuw' AND UserId = '14ocq7hp3by9ic95f7zqr1mjcw';
---
[c2] @TwizzyDizzy 2024-01-05T14:45:24Z:
Yes, of course, here you go:

**\d+ channelmembers;**

```

--------------------+------------------------+-----------+----------+---------+----------+-------------+--------------+-------------

 schemeguest        | boolean                |           |          |         | plain    |             |              |

 msgcountroot       | bigint                 |           |          | 0       | plain    |             |              | 
 urgentmentioncount | bigint                 |           |          |         | plain    |             |              | 
Indexes:
    "channelmembers_pkey" PRIMARY KEY, btree (channelid, userid)
    "idx_channelmembers_channel_id_scheme_guest_user_id" btree (channelid, schemeguest, userid)
    "idx_channelmembers_user_id_channel_id_last_viewed_at" btree (userid, channelid, lastviewedat)
Access method: heap
```

**select statement**

```

Thanks for confirming @TwizzyDizzy. This is an issue we are addressing. In the meantime you could technically fix it by updating the `NULL` `schemeguest` entries in those database rows. 

I'd check how many these are:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ChannelMembers WHERE SchemeGuest IS NULL;
````

And consider updating them with: 

```sql
UPDATE ChannelMembers SET SchemeGuest = false WHERE SchemeGuest IS NULL;
```

title: Users are deactivated but can log in when ID Attribute changes
need_summary: Whether a deactivated Mattermost LDAP user could still log in after an ID attribute capitalization change, with the answer anchored in the maintainer’s request to inspect the `authdata` field via the `SELECT authdata from users WHERE id = 'XYZ'` database query and the reproduced login/deactivation behavior.
security_topic: LDAP account deactivation and case-sensitive login behavior
question_text:
#### Summary
When the capitalization of the ID attribute value changes, the Mattermost account is deactivated on every LDAP sync and the session expired, but the user can still log in.

#### Steps to reproduce
Ubuntu 22.04
Mattermost 9.2.3
LDAP Sync from Active Directory with sAMAccountName as ID attribute and login ID attribute
1. sync existing AD user into Mattermost
2. log in as user into Mattermost
3. change the capitalization of sAMAccountName, i.e. Auser to auser
4. sync LDAP in Mattermost
5. user is deactivated in Mattermost and their session expired
6. log in with ANY capitalization of sAMAccountName as login ID attribute
7. user is successfully logged into their old account (i.e. retains their conversations and channel memberships)
8. sync LDAP again
9. user is again deactivated and their session expired
answer_text:
I'm still unable to reproduce the issue. Steps 1 to 5 work as described, but on Step 6 the login (with any capitalization) fails with an error. The error is thrown because Mattermost tries to create a new user account (because `sAMAccountName` does not match with the existing account), which fails because usernames are case insensitive in MM and hence, an account with the same username already exists (which is the "old", deactivated account)

To debug your issue further, could you please access your DB directly and get the `authdata` field from the deactivated account? Please run `SELECT authdata from users WHERE id = 'XYZ'` while replacing `XYZ` with the userID of the account.
thread_text:
ISSUE #25816: Users are deactivated but can log in when ID Attribute changes
Author: MrProteus
Date: 2023-12-26T01:06:58Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
When the capitalization of the ID attribute value changes, the Mattermost account is deactivated on every LDAP sync and the session expired, but the user can still log in. 
See also: <https://forum.mattermost.com/t/ldap-sync-deactivates-user-unexpectedly/5496>
<https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-11525>

#### Steps to reproduce
Ubuntu 22.04
Mattermost 9.2.3
LDAP Sync from Active Directory with sAMAccountName as ID attribute and login ID attribute
1. sync existing AD user into Mattermost
2. log in as user into Mattermost
3. change the capitalization of sAMAccountName, i.e. Auser to auser
4. sync LDAP in Mattermost
5. user is deactivated in Mattermost and their session expired
6. log in with ANY capitalization of sAMAccountName as login ID attribute
7. user is successfully logged into their old account (i.e. retains their conversations and channel memberships)
8. sync LDAP again
9. user is again deactivated and their session expired

#### Expected behavior
EITHER
change of ID attribute causes deactivation of account and user cannot log in anymore
OR
user can still log in and account is not deactivated (and their sessions don't expire)

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 
LDAP syncs after change of ID attribute value deactivate the account and expire all sessions; however, the user can still log in with their credentials and retain the same Mattermost account (i.e. keeps their conversations and channel memberships). They stay logged in until another LDAP sync is performed, upon which the log shows that the user is deactivated again (and logged out of any sessions). This matches the bevahior described in this forum post: <https://forum.mattermost.com/t/ldap-sync-deactivates-user-unexpectedly/5496>, however it is not clear to me whether the user in that case was still able to log in. 
It seems unintentional that a user that is marked as deactivated can log in. While it is stated in <https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-11525> that the ID attribute being case sensitive is intended, this behavior makes it hard to debug user reports like "I am logged out of my account every day". Alternatively, if a change in the capitalization of the ID attribute should still result in an user being able to log into the same Mattermost account, the account should not be deactivated and their sessions should not expire. 

#### Possible fixes
As a manual workaround, if the AuthData column value in the user database is changed to match the ID attribute including case, the Mattermost account is not deactivated on LDAP syncs anymore. 

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @hanzei 2024-01-05T10:36:31Z:
Thanks for the report @MrProteus.

I can reproduce that changing the `sAMAccountName` results in the old user getting deactivated. It's not clear to me if that is the expected behaviour. I need to confirm that with the Security team.

But I cannot reproduce that the user can log in using ANY capitalization of sAMAccountName. In my testing, after the `sAMAccountName`  was changed, the user could not log in using _any_ capitalization of sAMAccountName.

What Mattermost version are you using?
---
[c2] @MrProteus 2024-01-05T11:08:04Z:
We are using version 9.2.3, Database Schema Version: 113, Build Number: 6961628977. 
I just double-checked - the user can log in with different capitalizations even when `sAMAccountName `and `ID attribute value` match exactly (i.e. `sAMAccountName` and `ID attribute value` are `auser` but the user can log in using `Auser`, `AUSER` or `aUsEr`). 
---
[c3] @hanzei 2024-01-05T12:19:07Z:
Thanks for confirming the MM version. :+1: 

Just to double-check: Can the user log in with different capitalizations even after the `sAMAccountName` was changed in AD?
Another question: `sAMAccountName` is the value of `IdAttribute` in your MM config, right?
---
[c4] @MrProteus 2024-01-05T12:24:52Z:
Yes, the user can log in with different capitalizations both before and after changing `sAMAccountName` in AD. 
`IdAttribute` and `LoginIdAttribute` are both set to `sAMAccountName`. 
---
[c5] @hanzei 2024-01-08T12:28:52Z:
I'm still unable to reproduce the issue. Steps 1 to 5 work as described, but on Step 6 the login (with any capitalization) fails with an error. The error is thrown because Mattermost tries to create a new user account (because `sAMAccountName` does not match with the existing account), which fails because usernames are case insensitive in MM and hence, an account with the same username already exists (which is the "old", deactivated account)

To debug your issue further, could you please access your DB directly and get the `authdata` field from the deactivated account? Please run `SELECT authdata from users WHERE id = 'XYZ'` while replacing `XYZ` with the userID of the account.
---
[c6] @MrProteus 2024-01-11T16:01:55Z:
I started out with `sAMAccountName` in AD and `AuthData` being `auser` -- everything works as expected. I then changed `sAMAccountName` to `Auser` in AD and synced; inspecting the DB shows that `AuthData` and `Username` stay `auser`, `DeleteAt` now contains a non-zero value (that matches the value of `UpdateAt`).  

Logging in with `auser` (or other spellings like `AUSER`) succeeds, `AuthData` and `Username` are still `auser`; `DeleteAt` is again 0 and `UpdateAt` is increased. 

Just to rule this out as an error source, the `Id` column value in the DB is a random string starting with `etd73` - it is not related to `sAMAccountName` (but `IdAttribute` is set to `sAMAccountName` in config.json). 
---
[c7] @MrProteus 2025-04-03T20:01:51Z:
We have since migrated from MySQL to Postgres and upgraded Mattermost several times and cannot reproduce the error anymore. It's hard to confirm this now, but my suspicion is that a column in one of the tables in MySQL was set to case-insensitive - that would explain why database calls would still return matches, but string-comparisons in the Mattermost would not. 

Closing this issue as it can no longer be reproduced. 
---

title: Upgrading from 9.0.0 to 9.2.3 - Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files (Self-Host)
need_summary: Whether unsupported or malformed translation files could prevent Mattermost from starting during upgrade, with the concrete anchor being the linked Mattermost upgrade guide and the cited PR #24683 that introduced the invalid translation entries.
security_topic: upgrade-related translation-file loading failure
question_text:
While upgrading from 9.0.0 to 9.2.3 an error happened when starting the mattermost server 
"Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files"
answer_text:
I had the same problem from 9.0.0 to 9.2.3 because i forgot to run the command to remove the files as described in the upgrade guide in point 7 (https://docs.mattermost.com/upgrade/upgrading-mattermost-server.html)

Once i did that and coped the installation files again the error went away.

ISSUE #25584: Upgrading from 9.0.0 to 9.2.3 - Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files (Self-Host)
Author: Shimrockx
Date: 2023-11-30T09:21:30Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
While upgrading from 9.0.0 to 9.2.3 an error happened when starting the mattermost server 
"Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files"

#### Steps to reproduce
Install the 9.0.0 mattermost version entreprise edition on a bare metal server, and reproduce the upgrading steps from the documentation to upgrade to 9.2.3. [Upgrade Mattermost Server documentation](https://docs.mattermost.com/upgrade/upgrading-mattermost-server.html)

#### Expected behavior
Translation templates have errors when starting the server
Here are the error logs I noticed on the following languages: 
Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files: unable to parse translation #157 because template: Няправільны параметр {{. Імя}}.:1: function "Імя" not defined

Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files: unable to parse translation #180 because template: Ο χρήστης {{.User}} προστέθηκε στο κανάλι {{.Το Channel}}.:1: function "Channel" not defined

Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files: unable to parse translation #1124 because template: पासवर्ड के साथ बाहरी मैटरमोस्ट सिस्टम एडमिन को निम्नलिखित एईएस 256-बिट एन्क्रिप्टेड आमंत्रण भेजें। वे आमंत्रण स्वीकार करने लिए `{. Command}}` स्लैश कमांड का उपयोग करेंगे।

There are certainly many other languages involved, but I haven't tested them all.

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 
Full error logs :

```console
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]: Error: unable to load Mattermost translation files: unable to parse translation #157 because template: Няправільны параметр {{. Імя}}.:1: function "Імя" not defined
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]: map[id:api.context.invalid_param.app_error translation:Няправільны параметр {{. Імя}}.]
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]: Usage:
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   mattermost [flags]
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   mattermost [command]
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]: Available Commands:
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   db          Commands related to the database
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   export      Export data from Mattermost
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   help        Help about any command
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   import      Import data.
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   jobserver   Start the Mattermost job server
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   server      Run the Mattermost server
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   version     Display version information
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]: Flags:
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   -c, --config string   Configuration file to use.
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]:   -h, --help            help for mattermost
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost mattermost[177675]: Use "mattermost [command] --help" for more information about a command.
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost systemd[1]: mattermost.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Nov 30 08:45:28 mattermost systemd[1]: mattermost.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Nov 30 08:45:29 mattermost systemd[1]: Stopped Mattermost.
```

#### Possible fixes
The files concerned are in the i18n folder at the root of the mattermost installation.
You can solve the problems by renaming the language files concerned if you don't need them
example:
```shell
sudo mv i18n/be.json i18n/be.json.back
```
You can also correct the template yourself if you know the language, in order to contribute to the mattermost translation.

For my part, I made a copy elsewhere of the language files for my team and deleted all the other languages so as not to encounter this problem again.
```shell
cd {install-path}
sudo cp i18n/en.json ~/en.json
sudo rm i18n/*.json
sudo mv ~/en.json i18n/en.json
```

title: Implement Admin Warning Banner for Large Team Edition Installations (500+ Users) to alert of risks of large install
need_summary: Whether the large Team Edition installation warning banner was implemented as a security-risk notice, and the answer is anchored by the linked pull request https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/25797.
security_topic: warning banner for large Team Edition installations
question_text:
**Issue:** 
Mattermost Team Edition deployments with 500+ users aren’t protected from risks that could compromise the data and systems. 
 - Lack of advanced access controls, like multi-factor authentication, AD/LDAP user synchronization and sign-on, guest access controls, and granular team permissions, can create a scenario of access to sensitive data for individuals who should not have access.

- Inability to automate access controls creates risk of breaching data control policies.


**Proposed solution:** 
When an installation has 500 or more users, publish a warning banner across Mattermost visible to IT Admins. 
 
Text: Alert: Your system is at risk of disruptions that could severely affect your operations. We strongly recommend deploying Mattermost with advanced access controls.  [[Learn more](https://docs.mattermost.com/scale/high-availability-cluster.html)]
answer_text: A version of this was implemented with https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/25797. Mattermost is considering enforcing the limit. I recommend you comment on https://forum.mattermost.com/t/feedback-on-collaboration-for-mission-critical-work/17563 with your feedback.

title: Replace usage of LocalizedIcon in 'view_user_group_modal_header.tsx' with i/span tags
need_summary: Whether the back button’s accessible label should be moved from the icon to the parent button, using the react-intl translation key `user_groups_modal.goBackLabel` and the referenced Mattermost PR #25071 as the anchor.
security_topic: accessibility and aria-label placement for translated UI controls
question_text:
@M-ZubairAhmed I've a quick question 

` <button
                type='button'
                className='modal-header-back-button btn btn-icon'
                aria-label='Close'
                onClick={goBack}
            >
                <LocalizedIcon
                    className='icon icon-arrow-left'
                    ariaLabel={{id: t('user_groups_modal.goBackLabel'), defaultMessage: 'Back'}}
                />
            </button>`

The parent button you've specified has a generic aria-label in english named 'Close'
As our aim is to align with the react-intl translations, Should'nt we have an aria-label with the appropriate translate key inside the replacing <i> tag? 
Or if the parent button takes precedence,  in this case may be change and move the 
` ariaLabel={{id: t('user_groups_modal.goBackLabel'), defaultMessage: 'Back'}}`
into the parent button for more appropriateness 
Would like to know your thoughts on this
answer_text: @sapnasivakumar, that is the correct approach. Thank you for pointing it out. The aria-label on the button should have the translated 'Back' text, and the icon should not have any aria-label.

Author: mattermod
