Introduction

The purpose of this ticket is to eliminate the usage of LocalizedIcon in the `webapp/channels/src/components/view_user_group_modal/view_user_group_modal_header/view_user_group_modal_header.tsx` file. LocalizedInput currently encourages the use of a custom 't' function, which deviates from the standard practices of the react-intl. We are transitioning to align all our translations with the principles and methods of react-intl, ensuring consistency throughout our codebase.


Before you start:

- Assignment Confirmation: Comment on this ticket to express your interest in owning it. This will help prevent task duplication.
- Environment Setup: Ensure your development environment is up and running. Follow the setup guide https://developers.mattermost.com/contribute/developer-setup
- Analyse: Navigate to the file referenced in this ticket and examine its usage within Mattermost. Capture screenshots of where and how LocalizedIcon(s) are used; these screenshots will be helpful for future comparisons in the PR.
- Best Practices: Familiarize yourself with the best practices for contributing to the Mattermost https://developers.mattermost.com/contribute/why-contribute


Guidelines During PR Development:

- Replace FormattedIcon Usage: If the LocalizedIcon has a prop-named `component` with the value `span` replace the component with a `<span/>` tag. Otherwise, use `<i/>` tag to replace the LocalizedIcon.
- Component Type: Determine whether the component you're modifying is a functional or a class component.
- For functional components, utilise the `useIntl` hook from react-intl to replace any instances of the `t` function with `formatMessage` for the component's title or aria label.
- For class components, apply the `injectIntl` Higher Order Component (HOC) from react-intl to use the `formatMessage` function. Replace any occurrences of the 't' function with `formatMessage` for the component's title or aria label.
- Testing: Visually verify that the changes didn't cause any alterations in the app's UI. Ensure any relevant tests are updated to reflect the changes made during this PR. In some cases, you might need to update snapshots. You can run `npm run test – -u` from the "channels" folder to update them.


Checklist Before PR Submission:

- Screenshots for Comparison: Capture screenshots of the places where you replaced LocalizedIcon. These screenshots will allow for a quick visual comparison within the PR, helping identify any unintended UI changes. Remember to include the screenshot you took earlier for a before-and-after comparison. Screenshots also make it easier for QA to locate and review the changes made to components.
- PR Title Format: Write the title of your PR using the following format: '[MM-jiraTicketNumber] Write the ticket title here'.
- CI Checks: Ensure all Continuous Integration checks have passed successfully. The review process can only commence when all CI checks are green.

For reference, you can follow this PR https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/25071

title: Mattermost is violating the SAML 2 core specs in regard to Entity Identifiers
need_summary: Whether Mattermost’s SAML entity identifier must be accepted as a URI rather than a URL, with the answer anchored by the OASIS SAML 2.0 core spec and PR #24250.
security_topic: SAML entity identifier URI vs URL validation
question_text: Mattermost is incorrectly requiring a valid URL as an entityID (aka Issuer).  This violates the SAML2 core specs.  EntityID is defined in the specs as a URI, not a URL, and requiring this to be a valid URL breaks SAML integration with production IdPs that use a URI as an entityID.
answer_text: Hi @SphericalBastards, we have a PR waiting for one last security review here: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/24250
thread_text:
ISSUE #25041: Mattermost is violating the SAML 2 core specs in regard to Entity Identifiers
Author: SphericalBastards
Date: 2023-10-20T18:49:11Z
Labels: Bug Report/Scheduled for Release
State: closed

[c0]
https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/2f5ca43158bb1838c032eba9ff51c45f16910a6b/server/public/model/config.go#L3782

Mattermost is incorrectly requiring a valid URL as an entityID (aka Issuer).  This violates the SAML2 core specs.  EntityID is defined in the specs as a URI, not a URL, and requiring this to be a valid URL breaks SAML integration with production IdPs that use a URI as an entityID.  Many of these IdPs have been in production for over a decade.

See the following reference:
https://docs.oasis-open.org/security/saml/v2.0/saml-core-2.0-os.pdf

8.3.6 Entity Identifier

...The syntax of such an identifier is a URI of not more than 1024 characters in length..."

My gitlab authentication is broken for some users.
They get:

Most of users login fine.
answer_text:
I've managed to fix it.

Some users had a Password entry in the database on Users table.

I've emptied the Password field and users managed to login.

Nevertheless, some Users with Password entry where able to login without problem via gitlab.

title: Poor handling of expired session
need_summary: Whether the client’s blank pages and failed revalidation during server restarts are really caused by HTTP 429 rate limiting, with the answer anchored in the reported default `MM_RATELIMITSETTINGS_MAXBURST` behavior and the suggested workaround of increasing or disabling rate limiting.
security_topic: rate-limit handling during session revalidation after server restart
question_text:
When the server is restarted, or the sessions expire for whatever reason (see: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-server/issues/1105 ), the desktop client behaves erratically instead of handling the situation gracefully.

Expected behavior: User is asked to log in again and a new working session is established.

Observed behavior: The desktop client behaves erratically, with the display occasionaly going blank when switching teams, or various error messages being displayed, which are confusing to users (such as "rate limited" or "channel does not exist"). CTRL + SHIFT + R does not always resolve issue and has to be pressed repeatedly on different teams.
answer_text:
Basically the issue is that when you restart the server on production, all the desktop clients have to revalidate their session and with hundreds of clients doing this at once, when the server is restarted, triggers the RateLimit mechanism, hence the "limit exceeded" error message.

There are just a handful of clients on the test system and therefore the issue does not occur there.

However on production this boots random requests from clients in an unpredictable pattern and the client does not handle this well, as the user does not always get the error message and instead functionality just quietly fails and clients may even function normally and simply not recieve messages.

The workaround for this issue, is to either disable RateLiming on the server or increase the limits to the point that this reboot situation can be handled.

The proper solution would probably be to have the client handle HTTP error 429 more gracefully.

An alternative solution that would also work, would be to not immediately enable RateLimitng when a server is restarted, but delay it a few minutes to allow the initial spike to pass.

We observed the following:

After checking the inspector logs (on the Desktop and Web apps) we recognized - depending on the current server-load - HTTP 429 errors coming from the Mattermost instance. The workaround for this issue, is to either disable RateLiming on the server or increase the limits to the point that this reboot situation can be handled.

The proper solution would probably be to have the client handle HTTP error 429 more gracefully.

An alternative solution that would also work, would be to not immediately enable RateLimitng when a server is restarted, but delay it a few minutes to allow the initial spike to pass.

---

comments.author: moospit
comments.body:
Hi, we ran into the same issue with the Windows Desktop App and did some investigations.

We observed the following:

 - Desktop app throwing "limit exceeded" or
 - Desktop app immediately returning to login screen after succesful login
 - Reloading via `ctrl+r` / `ctrl+R` didn't work reliable

The Web/Mobile app was running without (visible) problems. Sporadic tests on the MacOS Desktop app showed no problems either.

After checking the inspector logs (on the Desktop and Web apps) we recognized - depending on the current server-load - HTTP 429 errors coming from the Mattermost instance. Digging a little deeper we found the `MM_RATELIMITSETTINGS_MAXBURST` default of `100` was exhausted quite fast, when logging in or reloading the Desktop *OR* the Web application (lots of requests during this phases).

After increasing the `MM_RATELIMITSETTINGS_MAXBURST` we don't see the exhausted rate-limit headers/HTTP 429 errors (yet) and the Desktop app seems to run stable. As i'm writing this the change is still fresh and we are still in testing, so i'll update if we see some other behaviour.

Interestingly the Web application also showed the HTTP 429 errors in the inspector, but did not show the same behaviour as the Desktop app (throwing errors/returning to the login screen).

Okay so 1 year later the test environment is set up.

I currently cannot reproduce the issue on this test environment, but reading your answers especially @moospit , I think I know what's going on and why this issue does not occur on the test system:

Basically the issue is that when you restart the server on production, all the desktop clients have to revalidate their session and with hundreds of clients doing this at once, when the server is restarted, triggers the RateLimit mechanism, hence the "limit exceeded" error message.

There are just a handful of clients on the test system and therefore the issue does not occur there.

However on production this boots random requests from clients in an unpredictable pattern and the client does not handle this well, as the user does not always get the error message and instead functionality just quietly fails and clients may even function normally and simply not recieve messages.


The workaround for this issue, is to either disable RateLiming on the server or increase the limits to the point that this reboot situation can be handled.

The proper solution would probably be to have the client handle HTTP error 429 more gracefully.

An alternative solution that would also work, would be to not immediately enable RateLimitng when a server is restarted, but delay it a few minutes to allow the initial spike to pass.

title: "Copy Link" and "Copy Text" commands for a post do not work with server v7.10.3
need_summary: Whether copying post links/text over HTTP was intentionally disabled because the Clipboard API requires HTTPS, with the answer anchored by the Clipboard API documentation linked in the maintainer reply.
security_topic: clipboard access restrictions on insecure HTTP origins
question_text:
#### Summary
Copy Link" and "Copy Text" command for a post does not work.
answer_text: This is actually working as designed as per the design of the Clipboard API (see here: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard). You will need to use HTTPS in order to work with the clipboard features we've added in Mattermost.
thread_text:
ISSUE #23978: "Copy Link" and "Copy Text" commands for a post do not work with server v7.10.3
Author: gucchy55
Date: 2023-07-10T00:33:19Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
"Copy Link" and "Copy Text" command for a post does not work.

#### Steps to reproduce
Server: v7.10.3 on Ubuntu
Client: v5.4.0 (on both Windows and Mac)
"Copy Link" and "Copy Text" commands do not put the post content into the clipboard.
It was no problem with server v7.9.1 and the same client version.

#### Expected behavior
The commands get to work again.

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @amyblais 2023-07-10T14:48:30Z:
An issue with the "Copy Link" is fixed via https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-52758 for v8.0.

I wasn't able to reproduce an issue with "Copy Text" in v7.10. Would you be able to help test it at https://community.mattermost.com/ (which is on the upcoming v8.0 release version) to see if it reproduces for you on the latest version?
---
[c2] @gucchy55 2023-07-10T21:18:29Z:
Thank you. In my environment, the copy commands do not put anything into the clipboard, which looks a different case from that of the mentioned ticket.
Anyway, I will try with v8.0 when it is released.
---
[c3] @gucchy55 2023-07-10T22:48:32Z:
With a desktop app (Windows and Mac), even when I select the menu "Copy Link/Text" for a post, it does not put anything into the clipboard. Is it an issue of the desktop app?
---
[c4] @amyblais 2023-07-11T01:54:38Z:
I wasn't able to reproduce it on v7.10.4 on Mac either on webapp or desktop app. If you're open to it, please help create an account at https://community.mattermost.com to see if the issue reproduces for you there. This is our active community server and on the latest version.
---
[c5] @gucchy55 2023-07-13T02:12:22Z:
I have roll-backed the server to v7.9.5, and it has no problem now. I will re-try the future version again. Thank you.
---
[c6] @f-velka 2023-07-14T01:17:24Z:
I have the same problem, and was able to reproduce it on Windows.

1. Launch mattermost v7.10.4 team edition using https://github.com/mattermost/docker on localhost:8065
2. Add the entry  `127.0.0.1 mattermost.example.com` to the hosts file
3. Access mattermost via `http://mattermost.example.com:8065` on browser
4. Try "Copy Link" or "Copy Text"

"Copy Link" and "Copy Text" work when I access via `http://localhost:8065`.
I think the [copyToClipboard](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/40ff77c9c6c2148e33a7fc5f49441b00bffd5c4c/webapp/channels/src/utils/utils.tsx#L1512) function isn't working properly when the context isn't secure and the Clipboard API is disabled.

---
[c7] @devinbinnie 2023-07-26T17:39:53Z:
This is actually working as designed as per the design of the Clipboard API (see here: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard). You will need to use HTTPS in order to work with the clipboard features we've added in Mattermost.
---
[c8] @f-velka 2023-07-27T14:42:24Z:
@devinbinnie 

As you mentioned, https is needed to use the Clipboard API, but in the previous versions such as v7.9.5, the "Copy Link" and "Copy Text" functions did work even with http, and it was thanks to the workaround below in [copyToClipboard](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/40ff77c9c6c2148e33a7fc5f49441b00bffd5c4c/webapp/channels/src/utils/utils.tsx#L1512), maybe.

```TypeScript
    // creates a tiny temporary text area to copy text out of
    // see https://stackoverflow.com/a/30810322/591374 for details
    const textArea = document.createElement('textarea');
    textArea.style.position = 'fixed';
    textArea.style.top = '0';
    textArea.style.left = '0';
    textArea.style.width = '2em';
    textArea.style.height = '2em';
    textArea.style.padding = '0';
    textArea.style.border = 'none';
    textArea.style.outline = 'none';
    textArea.style.boxShadow = 'none';
    textArea.style.background = 'transparent';
    textArea.value = data;
    document.body.appendChild(textArea);
    textArea.select();
    document.execCommand('copy');
    document.body.removeChild(textArea);
```
But it stopped working in v7.10.4.

I suspect that making or selecting the temporary text area before `document.execCommand('copy')` isn't working well, because when I select some text by dragging and then click "Copy Text", the selected text gets copied to the clipboard.


---
[c9] @syockit 2023-07-28T01:39:07Z:
While I can understand the rationale for not enabling clipboard over unsecured internet, it makes less sense for intranet (where usually https is not enabled) (also including VPN). Can we at least have it enabled for the desktop version?
---
[c10] @CJCombrink 2023-09-28T08:25:49Z:
@devinbinnie 
This is unfortunate for a server that is in an intranet.
Is it possible to at least put something in the clipboard or show an error indicating the issue?
Something like: "Copy not supported for http servers"
Not copying anything and no indication of the issue also feels like a bug. 
---
[c11] @syockit 2024-02-29T07:46:39Z:
I wrote an Edge extension that injects a script to create an empty object to replace `navigator.clipboard`, and appended a function to its `writeText` method that does the above workaround as posted by @f-velka, and it still didn't work. After some fiddling, I found that perhaps the textArea didn't get enough time to actually spawn for its `select()` method to properly work, so I enclosed everything after `appendChild` inside a `setTimeout` (with 100ms delay). I've also set `style.zIndex = 1` and `style.display = "block"`, though I'm not sure if they were necessary. Anyways, I guess enclosing that's what's needed to fix the code for the time being (until execCommand is removed).
---
[c12] @t-matz 2024-05-07T03:51:51Z:
It is now working in v9.6.1 with HTTP access. Did anyone fix this? 

FYI, I'm using Google Chrome(124.0.6367.119) as a client.
---
[c13] @marner2 2025-04-24T18:16:02Z:
This doesn't work for me on the latest server and mattermost client. I'm using an external reverse proxy for ssl. There's also no error, just a transparent failure.

title: Several ENV variables not locking out System Console UI fields when set
need_summary: Whether checkbox security settings in the Mattermost System Console can be locked out by environment variables, and the answer is anchored by PR !24151 plus the JIRA ticket MM-51521.
security_topic: environment-variable overrides failing to lock System Console settings
question_text:
There are a few environment variables which don't lock out the corresponding System Console fields when set:

  1. Allow untrusted connections

Setting this:
`MM*SERVICESETTINGS*ALLOWUNTRUSTEDINTERNALCONNECTIONS=`

Results in this:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5361908/226152016-7b4e0d91-dceb-4d2d-8748-88f947167897.png|alt="image")

For other settings, when the variable is empty the field is locked out with an empty value. This should behave the same way. It's a security issue for us because we use env variables to prevent system admins from changing any critical settings.

  1. Password minimum requirements

Setting this:

```MM*PASSWORDSETTINGS*NUMBER=true
MM*PASSWORDSETTINGS*SYMBOL=true
MM*PASSWORDSETTINGS*UPPERCASE=true
MM*PASSWORDSETTINGS*LOWERCASE=true
```

Results in this (the overrides are working but the fields aren't greyed out):

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5361908/226151931-b8cea1a5-f5c0-47b0-8032-1b9f3b8eabcb.png|alt="image")

  1. Session lengths

Setting these:

```M*SERVICESETTINGS*SESSONLENGTHWEBINHOURS=4320
MM*SERVICESETTINGS*SESSONLENGTHMOBILEINHOURS=4320
MM*SERVICESETTINGS*SESSONLENGTHSSOINHOURS=720
MM*SERVICESETTINGS*SESSONCACHEINMINUTES=10
```

Results in this:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5361908/226153128-96fbf97d-3a08-4332-bb89-5fd1faff68cb.png|alt="image")
answer_text:
For anyone reading this that doesn't open up the PR, of the 3 issues mentioned here only **2** is a real issue to be addressed.

1. Works as expected, in the provided example case `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_ALLOWUNTRUSTEDINTERNALCONNECTIONS=` which is the **wrong** environment variable - changing this to `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_ALLOWEDUNTRUSTEDINTERNALCONNECTIONS=` resolves the issue  (`ALLOWUNTRUSTEDINTERNALCONNECTIONS` -> `ALLOWEDUNTRUSTEDINTERNALCONNECTIONS`)

2. This is an actual issue - checkbox settings in admin do not have a solution currently - I have addressed this with [!24151](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/pull/24151)

3. Works as expected, in the provided example case `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_SESSONLENGTHMOBILEINHOURS=4320` was used - changing this to `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_SESSIONLENGTHMOBILEINHOURS=4320` (`SESSON` -> `SESSION`)

title: Threads view never finishes loading - only on desktop app (mobile app works with same user)
need_summary: Whether the desktop Threads API call is timing out because of the `extended=true` request option, as discussed in the Mattermost thread and server log error `pq: canceling statement due to user request`.
security_topic: desktop threads timeout and API parity
question_text: Is `extended=true` really not being the problem for Desktop? Can it not be fixed that way to bring Mobile and Desktop into parity?
answer_text: It looks like MM has its own timeout defined as `SqlSettings.QueryTimeout` which you're hitting. That seems to fit with the above error message since "canceling statement due to user request" seems to indicate that MM triggered the timeout, not Postgres
thread_text:
ISSUE #23690: Threads view never finishes loading - only on desktop app (mobile app works with same user)
Author: KlavsKlavsen
Date: 2023-06-09T06:01:17Z
Labels: Bug Report/Open
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
Threads view never finishes loading - only on desktop app (mobile app works with same user)

#### Steps to reproduce
desktop app 5.2.2 and then updated to 5.3.1 - issue is same.
server side is running: mattermost/mattermost-team-edition:7.9.0@sha256:edbbc9e28763e1dd94e6580e63cf5c9cc544022d4c5e2eb44b7eea6bcc044394 (on k8s)

#### Expected behavior
threads should show.

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 
for a long while - I could experience the same - then i switched away from threads view and back again and it would show immediately. for the last few days - it won't ever show - no matter how long I let it stay on "loading".
I see threads on my mobile app right now :(
I have tried clearing cache etc - and other colleagues - using same desktop app version does not have the problem.


--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @KlavsKlavsen 2023-06-09T08:54:07Z:
threads view works in a diff. team, on same server - which has a lot fewer messages/threads where I am in. But even then - same threads view - works for mobile.. so desktop must be doing something else - to make it never finish loading.
---
[c2] @KlavsKlavsen 2023-06-09T10:47:23Z:
I think the issue is the PG backend is not fast enough - so in that team I have "too many threads" - and it falls on the "timeout" - but client side does not show that - and offers no way to fix it.
I think maybe threads should be "limited" - so tables for threads is split into "monthly" tables - so smaller tables can be used (aka. DB partitioning) - as I don't care about last months threads really - so that would perform better - even if I have many threads..

some partitioning or perhaps caching with background-updating or other designs might help so it does not have to go through such a big heap to find my threads would help lower IO needs.. and oddly enough "there is a way" - to make it work already - as it works on mobile - which I suspect simply asks for a smaller subset of threads? [c11] @hmhealey 2023-06-29T14:32:57Z:
Sorry for the radio silence recently. We've been busy lately and haven't been able to get to this yet.

Your message made me wonder why mobile behaves differently. It's possible that it has more caching going on so you don't notice that the request is slow, but hopefully that's not the case.

I did notice that mobile's version of that API request doesn't have the `extended=true` option that's used there, so I assume that's the culprit. As best I can tell, that option changes whether or not it returns the users that participated in each thread. I don't know why that would cause the call to take that much longer since the query seems like it would be straightforward enough, but that's my best guess for a cause at the moment.

Perhaps we could see if changing that option changes anything? Could you try:

1. Going back to that view with the network tab open in the dev tools
2. Wait for the request to fail
3. Copy the request URL
4. Change `extended=true` to `extended=false` in it
5. Go to the JS console and run `fetch('<the modified url>')`
6. Watch the network tab for the new request

If it completes much quicker, we'll know for sure that that's the culprit.

And if that is the case and you're following any threads with a particularly large number of users participating, you could try unfollowing those from mobile to see if that helps the performance on the web.

[c16] @hmhealey 2023-06-30T15:18:15Z:
> I tried, and it failed the same way - after 30 seconds - getting a 500.

Damn, I was hoping that might be an explanation for the difference. Looking back at the logs, I think I've tracked down the error to [this line](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/channels/store/sqlstore/thread_store.go#L344) which occurs before we would've checked the value of `extended` anyway. The error I'm seeing repeatedly for the same user ID (which I assume is you) is a 500 error with:
```
GetThreadsForUser: Unable to get user threads, failed to get threads for user id=USERID: failed to fetch threads for user id=USERID: pq: canceling statement due to user request
```

I guess it's possible that the only reason mobile doesn't suffer from the same issue is that it's only fetching threads that have changed recently, not the older ones. Unlike the web app, it stores data when you close it, so it doesn't have to use the heavier API here.

> I tried going through list of followed threads on mobile and unfollowed a lot of 50+ reply threads.. (patience allowing.. got only around 20 - most threads are 2-30 - so its a HUGE list :)
It did not help.

I don't know if that would have as much of an effect, but it's definitely possible. I know I've been in longer threads before (the longest I remember was at least 200 posts), but that was usually surrounded by 2-5 post ones.

> I always changed postgresql timeout (from 30 to 50 seconds) - to see if that helped - but the request still stops after 30 seconds.. don't know if I have to restart mattermost client for this to take effect?

It looks like MM has its own timeout defined as `SqlSettings.QueryTimeout` which you're hitting. That seems to fit with the above error message since "canceling statement due to user request" seems to indicate that MM triggered the timeout, not Postgres

> Also - I found no way to "have it automaticly clean up old messages" ?
to avoid this growing for ever - I would not mind being able to set a "6 months" forget limit or something :)

That does exist, but it's only available with one of the levels of paid license. It's under the name Data Retention, but it's probably not visible in Team Edition which you're using

Anyway, I've asked around a bit to see if anyone more familiar with this code has more ideas since I tend to work closer to the frontend.

Once suggestion I did get was that you could try to run `VACUUM ANALYZE posts, threadmemberships` on the database to try to clean up those tables a bit. It was pointed out to me that this is such a heavy query because it relies joining the Posts, ThreadMemberships, and Threads tables together, and I do know that the Posts table at least is usually massive.

[c20] @KlavsKlavsen 2023-07-04T13:29:16Z:
or if query could be adjusted to only query for "last X period" - like 30 days or something in "normal query". that would help with this "not so big DB".

As I expect you know - I would recommend a Table partitioning scheme for larger scale - to avoid taking such a toll on a single DB. Partitioning makes query scaleable. (and lowers cost for partial queries - when you query on same as tables are partitioned on).

Partitioning is also what would enable a query client to f.ex. automaticly run "subqueries in partition queries" on seperate instances (ie. do scaling on read-only instances) etc. - and it allows for a high performance by needing to load only data "for the partition" when querying data - or whatever you partition on. This makes the query into multiple "smaller parallel" queries (hidden by partitioning support in PG) - which would most likely make it actually work better with same dataset on same hardware.

Currently the DB design seems built for vertical scaling - which means bigger and bigger db/IO/mem - much more expensive and has a ceiling - that horizontal scaling pushes much futher away.

If I had to guess, perhaps the request sometimes completes based on the server load, and mobile is able to handle that case a bit more gracefully since it stores the thread state between sessions.

Going back to the server-side issue though, I'm not much of a database guy, but if I had to guess, it seems like Ceph's performance when running a database may be what's causing these issues. I've never used it myself, but doing some quick googling, there's quite a few people recommending not running Postgres or other databases directly on it for performance reasons. There are some comments about using RBD instead of CephFS and tweaking the block size for it, but I have 0 experience with it so I don't know if that's even relevant here. It does seem like the general recommendation is to run the database on regular storage and only back it up to Ceph though.

[c30] @KlavsKlavsen 2023-08-17T06:47:40Z:
@hmhealey Well.. yeah - you can always "scale up" - on IO as well - and yes even a badly designed DB structure will often perform. That only works "so far" though - and then you're in  bad place and have no way to scale anymore (or you're paying a LOT for hefty IO. So running on Ceph - which IS slower IO than nvme etc. - just highlights something that WILL become a problem for larger mattermost instances - even on higher performance machines.

Our plan is to migrate all postgresql instances to local nvme and do clustering in postgresql to have redundancy/failover - that should help a lot - but that does not remove the badly designed sql structure/query here. (I've been working with high performance websites - 8k+ req/sec easily for many years - so I'm maybe a bit focused on 'high traffic paths' and performance - and not needlessly throwing IO/CPU/Memory at a problem (its like pissing your pants - it'll come back to be a problem and it'll be even worse :)

comments.author: hmhealey
comments.body:
Sorry for the radio silence recently. We've been busy lately and haven't been able to get to this yet.

Your message made me wonder why mobile behaves differently. It's possible that it has more caching going on so you don't notice that the request is slow, but hopefully that's not the case.

I did notice that mobile's version of that API request doesn't have the `extended=true` option that's used there, so I assume that's the culprit. As best I can tell, that option changes whether or not it returns the users that participated in each thread. I don't know why that would cause the call to take that much longer since the query seems like it would be straightforward enough, but that's my best guess for a cause at the moment.

Perhaps we could see if changing that option changes anything? Could you try:

1. Going back to that view with the network tab open in the dev tools
2. Wait for the request to fail
3. Copy the request URL
4. Change `extended=true` to `extended=false` in it
5. Go to the JS console and run `fetch('<the modified url>')`
6. Watch the network tab for the new request

If it completes much quicker, we'll know for sure that that's the culprit.

And if that is the case and you're following any threads with a particularly large number of users participating, you could try unfollowing those from mobile to see if that helps the performance on the web.

comments.author: hmhealey
comments.body:
> I tried, and it failed the same way - after 30 seconds - getting a 500.

Damn, I was hoping that might be an explanation for the difference. Looking back at the logs, I think I've tracked down the error to [this line](https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/channels/store/sqlstore/thread_store.go#L344) which occurs before we would've checked the value of `extended` anyway. The error I'm seeing repeatedly for the same user ID (which I assume is you) is a 500 error with:
```
GetThreadsForUser: Unable to get user threads, failed to get threads for user id=USERID: failed to fetch threads for user id=USERID: pq: canceling statement due to user request
```

I guess it's possible that the only reason mobile doesn't suffer from the same issue is that it's only fetching threads that have changed recently, not the older ones. Unlike the web app, it stores data when you close it, so it doesn't have to use the heavier API here.

> I tried going through list of followed threads on mobile and unfollowed a lot of 50+ reply threads.. (patience allowing.. got only around 20 - most threads are 2-30 - so its a HUGE list :)
It did not help.

I don't know if that would have as much of an effect, but it's definitely possible. I know I've been in longer threads before (the longest I remember was at least 200 posts), but that was usually surrounded by 2-5 post ones.

> I always changed postgresql timeout (from 30 to 50 seconds) - to see if that helped - but the request still stops after 30 seconds.. don't know if I have to restart mattermost client for this to take effect?

It looks like MM has its own timeout defined as `SqlSettings.QueryTimeout` which you're hitting. That seems to fit with the above error message since "canceling statement due to user request" seems to indicate that MM triggered the timeout, not Postgres

> Also - I found no way to "have it automaticly clean up old messages" ?
to avoid this growing for ever - I would not mind being able to set a "6 months" forget limit or something :)

That does exist, but it's only available with one of the levels of paid license. It's under the name Data Retention, but it's probably not visible in Team Edition which you're using

comments.author: hmhealey
comments.body:
Anyway, I've asked around a bit to see if anyone more familiar with this code has more ideas since I tend to work closer to the frontend.

Once suggestion I did get was that you could try to run `VACUUM ANALYZE posts, threadmemberships` on the database to try to clean up those tables a bit. It was pointed out to me that this is such a heavy query because it relies joining the Posts, ThreadMemberships, and Threads tables together, and I do know that the Posts table at least is usually massive.

comments.author: KlavsKlavsen
comments.body:
or if query could be adjusted to only query for "last X period" - like 30 days or something in "normal query". that would help with this "not so big DB".

As I expect you know - I would recommend a Table partitioning scheme for larger scale - to avoid taking such a toll on a single DB. Partitioning makes query scaleable. (and lowers cost for partial queries - when you query on same as tables are partitioned on).

Partitioning is also what would enable a query client to f.ex. automaticly run "subqueries in partition queries" on seperate instances (ie. do scaling on read-only instances) etc. - and it allows for a high performance by needing to load only data "for the partition" when querying data - or whatever you partition on. This makes the query into multiple "smaller parallel" queries (hidden by partitioning support in PG) - which would most likely make it actually work better with same dataset on same hardware.

Currently the DB design seems built for vertical scaling - which means bigger and bigger db/IO/mem - much more expensive and has a ceiling - that horizontal scaling pushes much futher away.

comments.author: hmhealey
comments.body:
If I had to guess, perhaps the request sometimes completes based on the server load, and mobile is able to handle that case a bit more gracefully since it stores the thread state between sessions.

Going back to the server-side issue though, I'm not much of a database guy, but if I had to guess, it seems like Ceph's performance when running a database may be what's causing these issues. I've never used it myself, but doing some quick googling, there's quite a few people recommending not running Postgres or other databases directly on it for performance reasons. There are some comments about using RBD instead of CephFS and tweaking the block size for it, but I have 0 experience with it so I don't know if that's even relevant here. It does seem like the general recommendation is to run the database on regular storage and only back it up to Ceph though.

comments.author: KlavsKlavsen
comments.body:
@hmhealey Well.. yeah - you can always "scale up" - on IO as well - and yes even a badly designed DB structure will often perform. That only works "so far" though - and then you're in  bad place and have no way to scale anymore (or you're paying a LOT for hefty IO. So running on Ceph - which IS slower IO than nvme etc. - just highlights something that WILL become a problem for larger mattermost instances - even on higher performance machines.

Our plan is to migrate all postgresql instances to local nvme and do clustering in postgresql to have redundancy/failover - that should help a lot - but that does not remove the badly designed sql structure/query here. (I've been working with high performance websites - 8k+ req/sec easily for many years - so I'm maybe a bit focused on 'high traffic paths' and performance - and not needlessly throwing IO/CPU/Memory at a problem (its like pissing your pants - it'll come back to be a problem and it'll be even worse :)

title: Wrong return value
need_summary: Whether the password-reset flow intentionally avoids revealing valid email addresses to prevent account enumeration and mailbox spam, as confirmed by the maintainer comments in the thread.
security_topic: email enumeration via password reset flow
question_text:
Please take a look at this function (link below)
Inside the function's body

Initially we find 1 user by given email
We do check if returning err is nil or not.
But in case it's NOT nill, we have to return that error instead of nil.

If an user enter wrong email, 
He would receive no reset email in the inbox and have no idea what was wrong about his action.

Thank you for reaching out, mr @agnivade, mr @jwilander
answer_text: Ah, thanks for clearing out my confusion! This is indeed to not disclose which emails are emails of valid users and which are not.

title: If Mattermost database is located on MySQL database cluster created by mysql-operator, database cluster fails to restart
need_summary: Whether the Focalboard-created `focalboard_file_info` table is incompatible with MySQL HA/group replication and needed a primary key, anchored by `dba.checkInstanceConfiguration()` and the documented `ALTER TABLE ... AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE KEY` workaround.
security_topic: database schema incompatibility causing MySQL InnoDB cluster restart failure
question_text: If Mattermost database is located on MySQL database cluster created by mysql-operator, database cluster fails to restart
thread_text:
ISSUE #23392: If Mattermost database is located on MySQL database cluster created by mysql-operator, database cluster fails to restart
Author: cerebrate
Date: 2023-05-15T23:56:24Z
Labels: Awaiting Submitter Action
State: closed

[c0]
#### Summary
If Mattermost database is located on MySQL database cluster created by mysql-operator, database cluster fails to restart

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Take a single-node Kubernetes cluster,
2. Install mysql-operator on the cluster using the Helm chart
3. Install mattermost-operator on the cluster using the Helm chart
4. Create a simple InnoDBCluster for Mattermost using the following definition:

```
---
apiVersion: mysql.oracle.com/v2
kind: InnoDBCluster
metadata:
  name: mattermostdb
  namespace: mattermost
spec:
  secretName: mattermostdb-pwd
  instances: 1
  router:
    instances: 1
  datadirVolumeClaimTemplate:
    storageClassName: ""
    volumeName: mattermostdb-pv
    accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
  tlsUseSelfSigned: true
```

(creating an appropriate private volume and database secret beforehand)

5. Create a Mattermost installation using the following definition

```
---
apiVersion: installation.mattermost.com/v1beta1
kind: Mattermost
metadata:
  name: mattermost
  namespace: mattermost
spec:
  version: 7.9.2
  size: 100users
  database:
    external:
      secret: mattermost-db-credentials
```

(creating appropriate external file store, database secret, and ingress beforehand)

6. Log on to and configure the resulting Mattermost instance, including the Boards plugin
7. Reboot the node.

#### Expected behavior

I would expect in this case that the database and Mattermost pods would all restart successfully post-reboot and the Mattermost instance would be accessible and functional.

#### Observed behavior (that appears unintentional) 

The Mattermost instance is inaccessible after reboot. Further examination shows that neither the Mattermost pod nor the router pod for the MySQL database cluster have been able to start. Examination of the logs of the mysql-operator pod finds the following error:

```
2023-05-15 23:31:13: Info: Validating InnoDB page size of instance 'mattermostdb-0.mattermostdb-instances.mattermost.svc.cluster.local:3306'.
2023-05-15 23:31:13: Info: Checking if performance_schema is enabled on instance 'mattermostdb-0.mattermostdb-instances.mattermost.svc.cluster.local:3306'.
2023-05-15 23:31:13: Info: Validating configuration of mattermostdb-0.mattermostdb-instances.mattermost.svc.cluster.local:3306 (mycnf = )

ERROR: Instance must be configured and validated with dba.check_instance_configuration() and dba.configure_instance() before it can be used in an InnoDB cluster.
2023-05-15 23:31:13: Error: Instance must be configured and validated with dba.check_instance_configuration() and dba.configure_instance() before it can be used in an InnoDB cluster.
[2023-05-15 23:31:13,865] kopf.objects         [ERROR   ] Handler 'on_pod_create' failed with an exception. Will retry.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/mysqlsh/python-packages/kopf/_core/actions/execution.py", line 279, in execute_handler_once
    result = await invoke_handler(
  File "/usr/lib/mysqlsh/python-packages/kopf/_core/actions/execution.py", line 374, in invoke_handler
    result = await invocation.invoke(
  File "/usr/lib/mysqlsh/python-packages/kopf/_core/actions/invocation.py", line 139, in invoke
    await asyncio.shield(future)  # slightly expensive: creates tasks
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.9/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 58, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/mysqlsh/python-packages/mysqloperator/controller/innodbcluster/operator_cluster.py", line 542, in on_pod_create
    cluster_ctl.on_pod_created(pod, logger)
  File "/usr/lib/mysqlsh/python-packages/mysqloperator/controller/innodbcluster/cluster_controller.py", line 699, in on_pod_created
    shellutils.RetryLoop(logger).call(self.create_cluster, pod, logger)
  File "/usr/lib/mysqlsh/python-packages/mysqloperator/controller/shellutils.py", line 93, in call
    return f(*args)
  File "/usr/lib/mysqlsh/python-packages/mysqloperator/controller/innodbcluster/cluster_controller.py", line 273, in create_cluster
    self.dba_cluster = dba.create_cluster(
RuntimeError: Dba.create_cluster: Instance check failed

```

#### Possible fixes

Needing to get the system back up and running rapidly, I elected to back up the database and attempt a manual patch. Using `dba.checkInstanceConfiguration()` in the database instance produced a report indicating that the `mattermost.focalboard_file_info` table did not have a primary key or equivalent column, a requirement for Group Replication, itself a requirement for running even a single-instance MySQL database using the MySQL Operator.

Running the following commands in the MySQL client attached to the database instance in question:

```
USE mattermost;
ALTER TABLE focalboard_file_info ADD COLUMN mysql_fix INT NOT NULL INVISIBLE AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE KEY;
```

followed by, in the MySQL shell attached likewise:

```
dba.checkInstanceConfiguration()
```

restored normal operation, allowing the database router and Mattermost pods to come up. After this, Mattermost (and Boards) appear to be operating normally.

I suggest the easiest fix is to add an official non-null unique key to the focalboard_file_info table.


--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @amyblais 2024-01-02T14:50:56Z:
Notes from a developer on the ticket:

This issue seemed to have been related to product behavior more so than the fact that it was running in k8s. In particular, this fix seems to indicate it was related to focalboard expectations:

```
USE mattermost;
ALTER TABLE focalboard_file_info ADD COLUMN mysql_fix INT NOT NULL INVISIBLE AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE KEY;
```

Focalboard has recently been moved to be community maintained. @cerebrate Is the issue still present on your end?
---
[c2] @cerebrate 2024-02-10T22:59:12Z:
Sorry for the delay in getting back to you.

The issue isn't still present on my end because, well, I applied that workaround and it was a one-time fix. :) I haven't set up a second Mattermost install using a mysql-operator back-end since then (I believe MySQL is deprecated now?), so I haven't experienced any recurrence of it myself.

I would agree that it's not a k8s-specific issue; it's a MySQL-installed-as-high-availability issue (which is the default even for a single-node deployment using mysql-operator, which is where k8s comes in), because one particular Focalboard-created table isn't compatible with HA-mode MySQL.

Go isn't one of my languages, alas, but as far as I can tell from a perusal of the mattermost/focalboard repository, the issue still exists in their data model. Maybe the best place to go from here, since Focalboard is now community-maintained, is to move this issue over to that repository?

---

title: insights cannot be disabled, env flag does nothing
need_summary: Whether setting the MM_FEATUREFLAGS_INSIGHTSENABLED environment flag in Mattermost’s docker-compose setup is enough to disable insights and whether the feature queries existing data only, based on the maintainers’ guidance in the thread.
security_topic: whether disabling insights via env flag is sufficient and what data it uses
question_text:
v7.10

Due to the performance decrease I want to disable this entirely unnecessary feature.

I set `MM_FEATUREFLAGS_INSIGHTSENABLED=false` in the `.env` where you would include other flags, but 'insights' still show up.

Also, please reconsider force-enabling playbooks etc. on next release. Why would we want to waste money running something we don't need? We use mattermost for its original purpose i.e. a more privacy friendly slack replacement.
answer_text: There is no excess metadata, insights just queries our existing data. Disabling vie env flag is sufficient
thread_text:
ISSUE #22994: insights cannot be disabled, env flag does nothing
Author: elandorr
Date: 2023-04-17T21:05:49Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
v7.10

Due to the performance decrease I want to disable this entirely unnecessary feature.

I set `MM_FEATUREFLAGS_INSIGHTSENABLED=false` in the `.env` where you would include other flags, but 'insights' still show up.

Also, please reconsider force-enabling playbooks etc. on next release. Why would we want to waste money running something we don't need? We use mattermost for its original purpose i.e. a more privacy friendly slack replacement.

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @elandorr 2023-04-18T17:23:58Z:
@amyblais Yes, full recreation. It doesn't show up in the console either:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/56206745/232853829-cd6913b6-4997-443a-b808-6aadb94a24a5.png)

---
[c2] @amyblais 2023-04-18T18:07:42Z:
You can add the following line under ``[Service]`` in your ``systemd`` service file for Mattermost: ``Environment="MM_FEATUREFLAGS_INSIGHTSENABLED=false"``. Can you help double-check if this helps?
---
[c3] @amyblais 2023-04-18T18:30:18Z:
Would you be open to posting about this on our [Peer-to-peer Help channel](https://community.mattermost.com/core/channels/peer-to-peer-help)? One of our devs or community members may have encountered this issue before and may be able to help troubleshoot this.
---
[c4] @elandorr 2023-04-18T20:19:46Z:
I'd rather not create yet another account, sorry. This is a default setup with all experimental stuff disabled, so I couldn't say much about it anyway.

My only idea was that the string in the changelog is wrong, but it seems to be correct.
---
[c5] @elandorr 2023-04-18T22:26:23Z:
Found the culprit @amyblais: Setting something in the .env of course only takes effect, if it's referenced in the compose.yml as well. Other vars like https://github.com/mattermost/docker/blob/main/docker-compose.yml#L61 are already there, the one to disable insights not. The 'insights' issue came up after it was modified last I think.

Works now, it's cleaner and faster without it. Will it wipe the excess metadata it might have collected from the db on its own?
---
[c6] @elandorr 2023-04-20T03:49:42Z:
@amyblais 

> Will it wipe the excess metadata it might have collected from the db on its own?

Would you let me in on that, please?
---
[c7] @amyblais 2023-04-20T12:24:01Z:
> > Will it wipe the excess metadata it might have collected from the db on its own?

@BenCookie95 @sbishel Would you know the answer to this?
---
[c8] @BenCookie95 2023-04-20T12:57:26Z:
> > > Will it wipe the excess metadata it might have collected from the db on its own?
> 
> @BenCookie95 @sbishel Would you know the answer to this?

There is no excess metadata, insights just queries our existing data. Disabling vie env flag is sufficient
---
[c9] @BenCookie95 2023-04-20T14:11:28Z:
> Thanks, Ben! Interesting there is any slowdown at all, then, if it's just another ordinary query.

Some of the queries are definitely quite heavy but they only run when you access the insights page directly. So unless you have a bunch of people constantly querying the insights page, turning it off might not make much of a difference
---
[c10] @elandorr 2023-04-20T15:45:42Z:
I see, thanks! The changelog mentioned performance issues - don't think anyone clicked that button more than once. It does feel speedier now. Maybe due to the restart.

If there's a chance you might consider not force-enabling the other features from the changelog, please do. Particularly db related activity or changes. To continue using MM, I had to make my own tool for privacy and file storage cleanup as MM inc. staunchly rejects GDPR for non-enterprise. The less often this has to be maintained/tested, the better.

(Saving memory/cpu is always useful, too.)

Cheers
---
[c11] @amyblais 2023-04-24T12:07:13Z:
I've shared this feedback with our team. They weren't sure what you meant by "...as MM inc. staunchly rejects GDPR for non-enterprise." Can you help share more details on this?
---
[c12] @elandorr 2023-04-26T01:03:34Z:
Can't believe we're doing that again, but I'll humor you. You full well know what it means, that topic has been brought up on your various forums and platforms for years.

But, if you forgot: I've asked about privacy/storage cleanup years ago. You acted as if you didn't understand basic tech to avoid having to give an honest answer. I explained over and over, this went on for a while. I was confused, as there was nothing that could be misunderstood. Then I realized you simply do not want, because you obviously have been ordered to shut this up, and I stopped bothering.

Many others tried before, it was silly of me to even bother. It's probably silly of me to reply right now, too, but I am a sucker for replies.

I still don't believe that's a good strategy - there are other tools out there, and someone who couldn't pay for enterprise before, wouldn't magically do so just because you hide a bare essential feature behind a paywall. He'll just move on begrudgingly or do what I did. Or 'crack' his way into EE, know a guy who went that route, but that's not an option for us. That's also not that helpful, as you have to keep up with that, too, then.

But you're likely an employee, so I understand you're just 'doing your job' and don't have a say in it.

This guy went through it all a long time ago: https://github.com/someone-somenet-org/mattermost-privileged
https://mattermost.uservoice.com/forums/306457/suggestions/15357861
https://mattermost.uservoice.com/forums/306457-general/suggestions/13851123-automatically-delete-the-oldest-attachments-when-a

> [someone ](https://mattermost.uservoice.com/users/200320383-someone)shared this idea  ·  **Jul 24, 2016**

Even 2015: https://mattermost.uservoice.com/forums/306457-general/suggestions/10007076-add-a-way-to-prune-reset-clear-channels?page=2&per_page=20


Plus like a dozen posts at least in other forums I don't have a link handy for.

The only way to use MM if you:

- do not have a magic millionaire storage black hole that lets you upload files ad infinitum
- need to actually delete messages, really delete, not just flag

is to write your own tool.

I've used 'someone''s  (best nickname ever) code as basis. But that's obviously not very reasonable. It took a long time and a lot of work since you can't just blindly copy paste. I verified every single query as best I could. But we've already set MM up and didn't want to start with something else from scratch. MM itself is also quite usable. It's far less res intense than the major competitor rocketchat last time we tried. Still bloated and not like IRC, but a good option. Corporate decisions be damned, I set out to write a tool, and did. 

That's what led me to ask for avoiding breakage, as it works pretty well right now. Not updating is not an option due to security updates, so best I can do is ask nicely not to break this. This situation is not something you research every week, so you have to start looking into it from (almost) scratch again, which eats unreasonable amounts of time. The 'someone' dude has enough free time, he works at a uni. Everyone else just moves on, normally. Not just because of the work, also for stability. As an admin, I cannot take maintenance responsibility for 3rd party code. I don't pretend to understand half a dozen large codebases, or even less be able to reliably and timely react to changes.

Real deletion should simply exist everywhere, and is even a GDPR requirement. Cleaning up storage is a must too - or how do you expect servers to exist? Maybe in your world having terabytes to throw around is normal, or you reinstall every couple months. Everywhere else, one has to have real deletion, expiration, retention settings, whatever you want to call it.

I think I even asked you before how we could potentially export/import all settings/users/chans/everything except messages to seriously automate a full reinstall to cleanly circumvent the problem. That's still stupid, 'hey, dear users, today I'll have to kill everything once more', but cleaner than manually messing with the db.

But who am I telling, of course you're aware of this. for 7 years now you've been pushing this strategy, after all.

I flat out asked you long ago, if you couldn't just ask the guy responsible for the db to informally acknowledge which parts of it can be touched safely standalone, or to maybe post a small script. It's absolutely trivial, if you know the codebase. It's just a hassle to outsiders. But... you know. You try to sell it in the enterprise, after all.

Someone else searching up all the posts regarding this issue must be laughing his butt off. From 2016 to 2023 a clown show. This 'freemium' corporate profiteering is a cancer to the open source community and if it were up to me, we'd simply use IRC and a phpbb again. Uses almost no resources, has legit deletion, zero telemetry issues, no privacy nightmares, etc.

But it has no emojis, duh. Must-have in 2023. /s (Not so sure even. Aren't they in unicode? Whatever.)

Cheers anyway, I guess it's just your job.
---
[c13] @olodar 2023-04-30T11:32:28Z:
> v7.10
> 
> Due to the performance decrease

Do you mean performance decreased after upgrade to 7.10? We have noticed after upgrade to 7.10 performance of client (webapp?) become extremely poor. Messages opens very slow and sometimes client can simply stuck with 100% core load. 
This problem is known?
---
[c14] @elandorr 2023-04-30T11:59:56Z:
@olodar I'm sorry, I didn't particularly take note. If you have a lot of content, building a clean-up tool based on the [repo linked](https://github.com/someone-somenet-org/mattermost-privileged) may be of benefit in general.

That'd be unrelated to this issue post though; you may want to create a new one.

To turn off the 'insights', add the var to the compose file either directly set to false, or blank there and set in the .env. But that shouldn't be related based on the response above.

I'll close this one as the original issue has been solved, and the ensued discussion regarding clean-up won't be solved anyway, as it has been rejected for 7 years.
---
